markers.name: DAO promoter
markers.description: The AOC1 rs10156191 T allele is associated with lower DAO enzyme production. DAO is a major enzyme that helps break down ingested histamine in the gut. T-carriers may experience elevated sensitivity to high-histamine foods, but symptoms and food tolerance vary.

markers.name: Thr105Ile
markers.description: HNMT helps break down intracellular histamine, particularly in the brain. The Thr105Ile T allele is associated with lower enzyme activity in some studies and may prolong intracellular histamine signaling; phenotype and exposures still matter.

markers.name: -13910C>T
markers.description: MCM6 regulates the LCT (lactase) gene. C/C is associated with adult lactase non-persistence in many European-ancestry studies, but symptoms and dairy tolerance vary. T-carriers often retain more lactase activity; genotype does not determine individual tolerance.

markers.name: Glu504Lys / ALDH2*2
markers.impact: Reduced aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 activity / acetaldehyde accumulation
markers.description: The ALDH2 rs671 A allele markedly reduces ALDH2 enzyme function. Carriers can accumulate acetaldehyde after alcohol exposure, producing flushing, tachycardia, nausea, headache, and higher alcohol-related tissue-stress risk when alcohol is consumed.

markers.name: Arg48His / ADH1B*2
markers.impact: Faster ethanol-to-acetaldehyde conversion / alcohol response modifier
markers.description: The ADH1B rs1229984 T allele encodes the His48 ADH1B*2 form, which increases ethanol oxidation to acetaldehyde. It is often associated with lower alcohol intake and alcohol-use-disorder protection, but can intensify acetaldehyde burden when ALDH2 clearance is weak.

markers.name: CYP1A2*1F / -163C>A
markers.description: CYP1A2 rs762551 is commonly used as a caffeine-clearance and CYP1A2 inducibility marker. The A allele is often treated as the inducible/fast-metabolism allele, but the effect is context-dependent and modified by smoking, hormones, liver status, and habitual caffeine use.

markers.name: ADORA2A 1976T>C / 1083T>C
markers.impact: Adenosine receptor sensitivity / caffeine sleep-anxiety response
markers.description: ADORA2A rs5751876 modifies sensitivity to caffeine's wakefulness-promoting, anxiogenic, and sleep-disrupting effects. It is most useful when interpreted alongside caffeine timing and CYP1A2 status.

markers.name: W143X / non-secretor variant
markers.impact: FUT2 non-secretor status / mucosal glycan and B12 context
markers.description: FUT2 rs601338 A/A produces non-secretor status for many individuals, altering ABO antigen secretion into mucosal fluids. Non-secretor status can influence norovirus susceptibility patterns and is associated with differences in measured vitamin B12 fractions.

markers.name: C282Y
markers.impact: HFE-related iron overload susceptibility when homozygous or compound heterozygous
markers.description: HFE rs1800562 A encodes C282Y, the major common HFE hemochromatosis variant. Homozygous C282Y has the strongest common genetic association with iron overload, but penetrance is incomplete and phenotype must be confirmed with iron studies.

markers.name: H63D
markers.impact: Mild HFE iron-loading modifier, especially with C282Y
markers.description: HFE rs1799945 G encodes H63D. Alone it usually has low clinical penetrance, but it can modify iron loading when combined with C282Y or relevant clinical context.

markers.name: C677T / Ala222Val
markers.impact: Reduced MTHFR activity / homocysteine context marker
markers.description: MTHFR rs1801133 T reduces MTHFR activity, especially in T/T individuals. Its practical value is as a folate/B12/riboflavin/homocysteine context marker, not as a standalone disease explanation.

markers.name: A1298C / Glu429Ala
markers.impact: Mild MTHFR activity modifier / one-carbon metabolism context
markers.description: MTHFR rs1801131 G has a smaller and more context-dependent effect than C677T. It should be treated as a weak one-carbon metabolism context marker, especially when combined with C677T and actual homocysteine/folate/B12 labs.

markers.name: A66G
markers.impact: Methionine synthase reductase / B12-dependent methylation context
markers.description: MTRR regenerates active methionine synthase, linking B12 status to homocysteine recycling. rs1801394 G has been associated with altered homocysteine in some cohorts, but effects are inconsistent and lab-dependent.

markers.name: A2756G
markers.impact: Methionine synthase / B12-dependent homocysteine recycling context
markers.description: MTR rs1805087 is a common methionine synthase variant studied in one-carbon metabolism. Evidence for individual prediction is inconsistent, so it should only be used as a weak context marker alongside B12, folate, and homocysteine labs.

markers.name: Pro259Arg / c.776C>G
markers.impact: Transcobalamin transport variation / active B12 context
markers.description: TCN2 transports the active fraction of vitamin B12 to tissues. rs1801198 G has been associated with B12-related biomarkers in some studies, but it should be interpreted only with measured B12, methylmalonic acid, and homocysteine.

markers.name: V175M
markers.description: PEMT rs7946 influences endogenous phosphatidylcholine synthesis and has been studied as a modifier of choline requirement and hepatic fat risk. Treat as a nutrition-context marker, especially when dietary choline intake is low.

markers.name: FADS1 intronic desaturase marker
markers.description: FADS1 rs174547 tags fatty-acid desaturase activity differences affecting conversion of shorter-chain polyunsaturated fats into long-chain omega-3/omega-6 derivatives. Useful for diet context, not as a disease claim.

markers.name: FokI
markers.description: VDR rs2228570 (FokI) changes the VDR start codon region and can alter receptor activity. It is useful only as a vitamin-D signaling context marker alongside measured 25(OH)D and clinical phenotype.

markers.name: BsmI
markers.impact: Vitamin D receptor regulatory variation / bone-mineral context
markers.description: VDR rs1544410 (BsmI) is a noncoding VDR marker often studied with other VDR variants for bone, immune, and vitamin-D-response context. It should be treated as a weak modifier rather than a direct deficiency marker.

markers.name: TCF7L2 intronic T2D-risk variant
markers.description: TCF7L2 rs7903146 T is one of the most replicated common type 2 diabetes susceptibility alleles and appears to affect insulin secretion/incretin biology. Use as a metabolic-risk context marker, not a diagnosis.

markers.name: FTO obesity-risk variant
markers.description: FTO rs9939609 A is a replicated obesity/adiposity-associated allele. In core interpretation, treat it as a satiety, energy-intake, and weight-management context marker, not as destiny.

markers.name: MC4R near-gene obesity/appetite marker
markers.description: MC4R rs17782313 C is a replicated common marker near MC4R associated with higher obesity susceptibility and eating-behavior differences. Interpret as appetite/energy-balance context only.

markers.name: Pro12Ala
markers.impact: PPAR-gamma insulin sensitivity and adipocyte differentiation context
markers.description: PPARG rs1801282 G encodes the Ala12 form. Many studies treat it as a metabolic-response modifier related to insulin sensitivity, adipocyte biology, and diet interactions, but results vary by ancestry and phenotype.

markers.name: Arg325Trp
markers.impact: Zinc transporter 8 / insulin granule biology and T2D risk
markers.description: SLC30A8 rs13266634 C is the common Arg325 allele associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk in multiple studies, likely through beta-cell zinc transport and insulin processing context.

markers.name: I148M
markers.impact: Hepatic fat accumulation and fatty-liver severity modifier
markers.description: PNPLA3 rs738409 G encodes I148M and is one of the strongest common genetic modifiers of fatty liver susceptibility and progression risk. Use with liver enzymes, metabolic status, alcohol exposure, and imaging.

markers.name: Thr92Ala
markers.impact: Local T4-to-T3 conversion modifier / thyroid hormone signaling context
markers.description: DIO2 rs225014 A encodes the Ala92 form and has been studied as a modifier of intracellular T3 production and levothyroxine response in some cohorts. Interpret only with thyroid labs and symptoms.

markers.name: R620W
markers.description: PTPN22 rs2476601 A encodes the R620W allele, one of the stronger common autoimmune susceptibility variants in European ancestry populations, including thyroid autoimmunity, type 1 diabetes, and rheumatoid arthritis contexts.

markers.name: Ala16Val
markers.description: SOD2 rs4880 alters the mitochondrial targeting sequence of manganese superoxide dismutase. The T/Val allele is often interpreted as a modifier of mitochondrial antioxidant handling, but clinical effects are heterogeneous.

markers.name: Pro198Leu
markers.description: GPX1 rs1050450 T encodes the Leu198 form and has been associated with reduced GPx1 enzyme activity in some studies. Useful as a selenium/antioxidant context marker, not as disease prediction.

markers.name: C609T / Pro187Ser
markers.impact: Reduced NQO1 quinone detoxification enzyme stability/activity
markers.description: NQO1 rs1800566 T encodes Pro187Ser, which substantially reduces NQO1 protein stability and enzyme activity, especially in T/T carriers. Use as a detoxification/redox context marker, not as a cancer prediction marker.

markers.name: Ile105Val
markers.impact: Glutathione S-transferase P1 substrate handling modifier
markers.description: GSTP1 rs1695 G encodes the Val105 form and can alter GSTP1 catalytic activity and substrate handling. Useful as a broad detoxification-context marker, but disease associations are inconsistent.

markers.name: Asp299Gly
markers.description: TLR4 rs4986790 G encodes Asp299Gly and has been studied as a modifier of LPS/TLR4 signaling and innate immune response. Associations vary, so use only as a low-confidence inflammatory-response context marker.

markers.name: -174G>C promoter
markers.description: IL6 rs1800795 is a promoter variant studied in inflammatory signaling and CRP/cytokine contexts. Because associations vary by ancestry and condition, treat as a weak inflammatory-tone context marker only.

markers.name: TNF-alpha -308G>A promoter
markers.description: TNF rs1800629 A is a promoter variant studied in TNF-alpha expression and inflammatory disease susceptibility. It is too nonspecific for diagnosis and should only be used as a low-confidence inflammatory-context marker.

markers.name: ACE I/D proxy / 2350A>G synonymous marker
markers.impact: ACE activity and vascular-tone context marker
markers.description: ACE rs4343 is commonly used as a SNP proxy for ACE I/D-related ACE activity differences. In core interpretation, it belongs only as a blood-pressure/endurance-response context marker.

markers.name: CYP2D6*4
markers.description: CYP2D6*4 is a well-established no-function allele. An A/A result at rs3892097 may be consistent with a poor-metabolizer diplotype when the rest of the CYP2D6 genotype supports it; full clinical PGx interpretation is required before applying drug guidance.

markers.name: CYP2C9*3
markers.description: The CYP2C9*3 variant significantly reduces enzymatic clearance. C-carriers may experience slower clearance and higher systemic levels of warfarin, statins, and common NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or celecoxib).

markers.name: CYP2C9*2
markers.description: CYP2C9*2 (rs1799853) is a common coding variant that reduces enzyme activity. Individuals carrying T-alleles metabolize warfarin, phenytoin, and NSAIDs slower than typical *1/*1 individuals.

markers.name: CYP2C19*17
markers.description: The CYP2C19*17 variant is associated with increased transcription. T-carriers are ultra-rapid metabolizers of SSRI antidepressants (like escitalopram and sertraline) and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), potentially leading to lower drug efficacy at standard doses.

markers.name: CYP2C19*2
markers.impact: Reduced CYP2C19 enzyme activity (loss of function)
markers.description: CYP2C19*2 is a common loss-of-function allele. Homozygous carriers have poor metabolizer status, leading to reduced activation of clopidogrel and slow clearance of certain SSRIs and PPIs.

markers.name: CYP2C19*3
markers.impact: Reduced CYP2C19 enzyme activity (loss of function)
markers.description: CYP2C19*3 is a no-function allele that introduces a premature stop codon and is observed more often in East Asian populations. Homozygosity or compound heterozygosity may support a poor-metabolizer phenotype, but the complete clinical diplotype is required.

markers.name: Val174Ala
markers.impact: Impaired statin transport / elevated systemic statin levels
markers.description: The SLCO1B1 Val174Ala C allele decreases the transport of statins (especially simvastatin) into the liver, resulting in higher blood concentrations and a significantly higher risk of statin-induced myopathy (muscle pain).

markers.name: -1639G>A
markers.description: The VKORC1 -1639G>A promoter variant decreases VKORC1 expression. Individuals with the A allele require significantly lower therapeutic warfarin doses to avoid bleeding risks.

markers.name: Val433Met
markers.impact: Altered Vitamin K metabolism / higher warfarin dose requirements
markers.description: The Met433 variant reduces CYP4F2 activity, causing lower breakdown of Vitamin K. Consequently, T-carriers require slightly higher doses of warfarin to achieve anticoagulation.

markers.name: CYP3A5*3
markers.description: The CYP3A5*3 C-allele is associated with altered splicing. A *3/*3 result is often consistent with a CYP3A5 non-expresser phenotype and may reduce clearance of drugs such as tacrolimus; use the complete clinical diplotype and drug-specific guidance.

markers.name: CYP2B6*6
markers.description: The CYP2B6*6 variant is associated with reduced enzyme activity and expression. Carriers of the T allele may experience slow clearance of bupropion (Wellbutrin), methadone, and efavirenz, leading to elevated drug exposure.

markers.name: Gln141Lys
markers.impact: Impaired drug transport / statin toxicity risk / gout susceptibility
markers.description: The ABCG2 Gln141Lys T allele impairs active transport of substrates, resulting in elevated systemic levels of statins (specifically rosuvastatin) and reduced renal uric acid export, increasing gout risk.

markers.name: DPYD*2A
markers.impact: Severe fluorouracil / capecitabine toxicity risk (loss of function)
markers.description: DPYD*2A is a critical splice-site variant leading to complete lack of DPD enzyme activity. Carriers of the A allele are at extreme risk of life-threatening toxicity (neutropenia, severe mucosal inflammation) if treated with standard doses of fluorouracil or capecitabine.

markers.name: rs55886062 / I560S
markers.impact: Severe fluorouracil / capecitabine toxicity risk (loss of function)
markers.description: The rare DPYD I560S allele can substantially reduce DPD activity and increase fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk. A C-allele result requires clinical DPYD confirmation and oncology/pharmacogenomic guidance before 5-FU or capecitabine exposure.

markers.name: rs67376798 / Y186C
markers.impact: Severe fluorouracil / capecitabine toxicity risk (loss of function)
markers.description: The DPYD Y186C variant may reduce DPD activity and is associated with increased fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk in clinical studies. An A-allele result requires clinical DPYD interpretation before 5-FU-based chemotherapy.

markers.name: TPMT*3B / TPMT*3A component (A154T)
markers.description: rs1800460 is the TPMT*3B-defining A154T component and, when paired with rs1142345, forms TPMT*3A. It reduces TPMT activity and increases thiopurine myelosuppression risk. Use clinical TPMT genotype/phenotype confirmation.

markers.name: TPMT*3C / TPMT*3A component (A719G)
markers.description: rs1142345 helps identify TPMT*3C and, when paired with rs1800460, is part of TPMT*3A. The resulting TPMT diplotype may reduce enzyme activity and increase thiopurine toxicity risk; use clinical TPMT genotype/phenotype confirmation.

markers.name: rs116855232 / *3
markers.description: NUDT15 rs116855232 is a major loss-of-function allele, highly prevalent in East Asian populations. Homozygotes or compound heterozygotes develop severe leucopenia and alopecia under thiopurines, independent of TPMT status.

markers.name: PGx raw-DNA non-actionability rule
markers.impact: Prevents medication changes from consumer raw DNA
markers.description: Raw DNA can flag possible PGx issues but is not a clinical PGx report. Do not start, stop, dose-adjust, or avoid medications from this file without clinician/pharmacist review and clinical confirmation when relevant.

markers.name: CYP2D6 star-allele/CNV/hybrid interpreter required
markers.impact: CYP2D6 metabolizer phenotype cannot be inferred from one SNP
markers.description: CYP2D6 requires star-allele diplotype, copy-number, deletion/duplication, and hybrid allele interpretation. Single SNPs such as *4 or *10 are incomplete.

markers.name: HLA drug hypersensitivity typing guardrail
markers.impact: HLA-mediated severe cutaneous adverse reaction risk domain
markers.description: HLA-B*15:02, HLA-A*31:01, HLA-B*57:01, and HLA-B*58:01 are clinically actionable for specific drugs, but SNP proxies are not enough. Require clinical HLA typing.

markers.name: CYP2D6*10 component
markers.description: CYP2D6*10 is a decreased-function allele common in East Asian populations. Interpret only as part of a full CYP2D6 diplotype.

markers.name: CYP2D6*41 component
markers.description: CYP2D6*41 is a decreased-function allele component. Use in a full star-allele interpreter only.

markers.name: CYP2D6*3 frameshift component
markers.description: CYP2D6*3 is a no-function allele. Indel calls from consumer data require confirmation and full diplotype context.

markers.name: CYP2D6*6 deletion component
markers.description: CYP2D6*6 is a no-function allele component. Confirm clinically and integrate with diplotype/CNV.

markers.name: CYP2D6*17 component
markers.description: CYP2D6*17 is a decreased-function allele component more frequent in African ancestry populations. Use only with full diplotype calling.

markers.name: CYP2D6*5 whole-gene deletion
markers.impact: No CYP2D6 enzyme from deleted allele
markers.description: CYP2D6*5 is a whole-gene deletion causing a no-function allele. It cannot be inferred reliably from ordinary SNP data.

markers.name: CYP2D6 allele duplication/multiplication
markers.impact: Potential increased CYP2D6 activity when active allele duplicated
markers.description: CYP2D6 duplications can cause ultrarapid metabolism when functional alleles are multiplied. SNP-only raw data usually cannot resolve this.

markers.name: CYP2C19*4
markers.description: CYP2C19*4 is a no-function allele. It should be integrated into CYP2C19 diplotype interpretation for clopidogrel, PPIs, SSRIs, and other substrates.

markers.name: CYP2C19*5
markers.description: CYP2C19*5 is a rare no-function allele. Confirm before clinical use.

markers.name: CYP2C19*6
markers.description: CYP2C19*6 is a no-function allele component. Use only in validated PGx calling.

markers.name: CYP2C19*7
markers.description: CYP2C19*7 is a splice/no-function allele. Confirm clinically.

markers.name: CYP2C19*8
markers.description: CYP2C19*8 is a no-function allele. Integrate into diplotype only after clinical confirmation.

markers.name: CYP2C9*5
markers.description: CYP2C9*5 reduces CYP2C9 function and is relevant to warfarin, phenytoin, and NSAID PGx in populations where covered.

markers.name: CYP2C9*6
markers.description: CYP2C9*6 is a reduced/no-function allele relevant to warfarin and other CYP2C9 substrates. Confirm clinically.

markers.name: CYP2C9*8
markers.description: CYP2C9*8 reduces enzyme activity and is important in some ancestries. Use in a full CYP2C9 diplotype.

markers.name: CYP2C9*11
markers.description: CYP2C9*11 is a decreased-function allele. Use only with clinical PGx interpretation.

markers.name: Asn130Asp / SLCO1B1*1B component
markers.description: SLCO1B1 rs2306283 contributes to statin transporter haplotypes and can modify statin exposure context. Interpret with rs4149056 and statin-specific guidance.

markers.name: SLCO1B1 reduced-function haplotype component
markers.description: SLCO1B1 rs11045819 contributes to reduced transporter function haplotypes for some drugs. Use in clinical haplotype context.

markers.name: SLCO1B1 statin myopathy GWAS proxy
markers.description: rs4363657 is a proxy marker historically associated with simvastatin myopathy risk near SLCO1B1. Prefer direct star-allele/haplotype interpretation.

markers.name: DPYD HapB3 / c.1129-5923C>G tag
markers.impact: Reduced DPD activity / fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk
markers.description: DPYD HapB3 is a clinically relevant decreased-function haplotype for fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk. Confirm before acting.

markers.name: DPYD HapB3 component
markers.description: rs56038477 is part of DPYD HapB3 context. Use validated DPYD haplotype calling before any clinical action.

markers.name: TPMT*2
markers.impact: Reduced TPMT activity / thiopurine toxicity risk
markers.description: TPMT*2 reduces TPMT activity and can increase thiopurine myelosuppression risk. Interpret with TPMT/NUDT15 phenotype.

markers.name: NUDT15*2 component
markers.impact: Reduced NUDT15 activity / thiopurine toxicity risk
markers.description: NUDT15 decreased/no-function variants increase thiopurine intolerance risk. Use clinical PGx confirmation and CPIC guidance.

markers.name: NUDT15*6 candidate/component
markers.impact: Reduced NUDT15 activity / thiopurine toxicity risk
markers.description: NUDT15 rare alleles can reduce enzyme activity and increase thiopurine toxicity risk. Confirm clinically.

markers.name: UGT1A1*28 promoter TA7 repeat
markers.impact: Reduced UGT1A1 glucuronidation / irinotecan and bilirubin context
markers.description: UGT1A1*28 reduces UGT1A1 expression and is relevant to irinotecan toxicity and Gilbert syndrome context. VNTR/promoter repeat requires appropriate testing.

markers.name: UGT1A1*28 tag SNP
markers.impact: Reduced UGT1A1 expression proxy / bilirubin-irinotecan context
markers.description: rs887829 tags UGT1A1*28 in many populations and is associated with bilirubin levels, but direct UGT1A1 repeat testing is preferred for clinical decisions.

markers.name: UGT1A1*6 Gly71Arg
markers.impact: Reduced UGT1A1 activity / irinotecan toxicity risk
markers.description: UGT1A1*6 reduces glucuronidation and is important in East Asian ancestry for irinotecan/bilirubin PGx.

markers.name: HLA-B*57:01 abacavir hypersensitivity allele
markers.description: HLA-B*57:01 is clinically actionable for abacavir hypersensitivity prevention. Requires clinical HLA typing.

markers.name: HLA-B*15:02 carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine SCAR allele
markers.impact: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction risk with aromatic anticonvulsants
markers.description: HLA-B*15:02 is clinically actionable for carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine severe cutaneous adverse reaction risk, especially in relevant ancestries. Requires clinical HLA typing.

markers.name: HLA-A*31:01 carbamazepine hypersensitivity allele
markers.description: HLA-A*31:01 is associated with carbamazepine hypersensitivity reactions. Requires clinical HLA typing for action.

markers.name: HLA-B*58:01 allopurinol SCAR allele
markers.impact: Allopurinol severe cutaneous adverse reaction risk
markers.description: HLA-B*58:01 is clinically actionable for allopurinol severe cutaneous adverse reaction risk. Requires clinical HLA typing.

markers.name: G6PD A- 202G>A component
markers.impact: Reduced G6PD activity / oxidative hemolysis drug risk
markers.description: G6PD deficiency can cause hemolysis with rasburicase and other oxidative stressors. rs1050828 is one component; phenotype/enzyme testing may be needed.

markers.name: G6PD A- 376A>G component
markers.description: rs1050829 contributes to G6PD A/A- haplotypes. Interpret with rs1050828 and/or enzyme activity.

markers.name: G6PD deficiency clinical testing panel
markers.description: G6PD deficiency is clinically actionable for rasburicase and oxidant-drug exposure. Use clinical genotype or enzyme assay, not limited SNPs.

markers.name: Butyrylcholinesterase K variant
markers.description: BCHE variants can contribute to prolonged apnea after succinylcholine or mivacurium. Clinical enzyme/dibucaine testing is preferred for anesthesia risk.

markers.name: Butyrylcholinesterase deficiency clinical panel
markers.description: Pathogenic BCHE variants can cause prolonged paralysis/apnea after succinylcholine/mivacurium. Confirm clinically.

markers.name: Malignant hyperthermia susceptibility panel
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic RYR1/CACNA1S variants can indicate malignant hyperthermia susceptibility. This is high-stakes and requires clinical confirmation.

markers.name: NAT2*5 component
markers.description: NAT2 slow acetylator status affects isoniazid and some other drug/toxin metabolism. Requires haplotype interpretation.

markers.name: NAT2*5/*6 component
markers.description: NAT2 rs1801280 contributes to slow acetylator haplotypes. Use only in full haplotype context.

markers.name: NAT2*6 component
markers.description: NAT2*6 contributes to slow acetylator status relevant to isoniazid toxicity/efficacy context.

markers.name: NAT2*7 component
markers.description: NAT2*7 contributes to slow acetylator status. Interpret clinically as a haplotype.

markers.name: CYP3A4*22
markers.description: CYP3A4*22 reduces CYP3A4 expression and can affect exposure to some CYP3A substrates. Clinical utility is drug-specific and evolving.

markers.name: CYP2C8*3 component R139K
markers.description: CYP2C8*3 can alter metabolism of some NSAIDs and oncology drugs such as paclitaxel. Use with drug-specific guidance.

markers.name: CYP2C8*3 component K399R
markers.description: rs11572080 is part of CYP2C8*3 haplotype. Interpret only with haplotype/drug context.

markers.name: CYP2C8*4
markers.description: CYP2C8*4 can modify metabolism for selected CYP2C8 substrates. Clinical utility is drug-specific.

markers.name: Interferon lambda treatment-response marker
markers.description: IFNL3/IFNL4-region variation historically influenced interferon-based hepatitis C treatment response. Relevance is reduced in the direct-acting antiviral era.

markers.name: IFNL4 ss469415590 ΔG/TT
markers.description: IFNL4 functional variation is linked to interferon-era HCV treatment response and viral clearance. Use only in current clinical context.

markers.name: CES1 dabigatran exposure marker
markers.description: CES1 rs2244613 has been associated with dabigatran active metabolite exposure and bleeding risk in some studies. Clinical implementation is not universal.

markers.name: CES1 G143E
markers.impact: Reduced CES1 activity / methylphenidate and ester-drug context
markers.description: CES1 G143E reduces CES1 activity and can affect methylphenidate and ester prodrug exposure. Confirm before clinical use.

markers.name: CYP2A6*2
markers.description: CYP2A6 decreased-function variants affect nicotine metabolism and smoking cessation pharmacology research. Clinical implementation varies.

markers.name: CYP2A6*4 whole-gene deletion
markers.description: CYP2A6 deletion can strongly reduce nicotine metabolism, but CNV testing is required.

markers.name: CYP2E1*5B promoter marker
markers.description: CYP2E1 metabolizes ethanol and small solvents; rs2031920 is a research marker with limited clinical PGx utility.

markers.name: Arg213His
markers.description: SULT1A1 variants can affect sulfation of hormones and some drugs, but clinical implementation is limited.

markers.name: KCNQ1 intron variant
markers.description: KCNQ1 regulates potassium channels in pancreatic beta cells. The rs2237897 A allele is a robust marker associated with impaired insulin secretion following glucose loads, carrying a modest risk signal for type 2 diabetes.

markers.name: Glu23Lys
markers.description: KCNJ11 rs5219 (E23K variant, T allele) keeps the pancreatic beta-cell potassium channel open longer, decreasing insulin secretion in response to glucose.

markers.name: GCKR intron variant
markers.impact: Altered glucokinase activity / triglyceride-glucose balance shift
markers.description: GCKR regulates glucokinase in the liver. The T allele is associated with lower fasting glucose but higher fasting triglycerides, illustrating a metabolic lipid-glucose partition tradeoff.

markers.name: -1131T>C
markers.impact: Reduced APOA5 expression / elevated fasting triglycerides
markers.description: APOA5 rs662799 C allele is strongly associated with elevated serum triglycerides due to reduced clearing of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins.

markers.name: Ser447Ter
markers.impact: Altered Lipoprotein Lipase activity / triglyceride clearance
markers.description: LPL rs328 G (Ser44Ter) introduces a premature stop and has been associated with increased LPL activity, lower triglycerides, and higher HDL in some studies. Lipid phenotype and clinical context remain important.

markers.name: TaqIB polymorphism
markers.impact: Altered cholesteryl ester transfer protein activity
markers.description: The A (TaqIB B2) allele of rs708272 is linked to decreased CETP expression, which increases protective HDL cholesterol levels.

markers.name: rs10455872 promoter variant
markers.description: LPA rs10455872 is a robust promoter-associated SNP driving elevated levels of Lipoprotein(a). High Lp(a) levels are an independent, highly genetically determined risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

markers.name: Ile4399Met
markers.description: The rs3798220 C-allele is associated with smaller apolipoprotein(a) size isoforms, which are cleared slower, leading to elevated Lp(a) levels.

markers.name: Metabolic raw-DNA non-diagnostic rule
markers.description: Common metabolic variants are small-effect modifiers. Diabetes, insulin resistance, obesity, dyslipidemia, gout, and fatty liver require labs, phenotype, medications, diet, body composition, and clinician interpretation.

markers.name: Type 2 diabetes PRS module
markers.description: T2D genetics involves hundreds of loci and multiple mechanistic clusters. Use only validated PRS with ancestry/platform calibration and lab context.

markers.name: BMI/obesity PRS module
markers.description: Common obesity genetics strongly involves CNS appetite/energy regulation, but PRS does not determine body weight or individual behavior.

markers.name: MTNR1B intron variant
markers.impact: Melatonin receptor / fasting glucose and insulin secretion context
markers.description: MTNR1B rs10830963 G is associated with higher fasting glucose and altered insulin secretion, especially with circadian-melatonin timing context.

markers.name: CDKAL1 T2D locus
markers.description: CDKAL1 variants are replicated T2D loci affecting beta-cell insulin secretion context.

markers.name: 9p21 T2D locus
markers.description: CDKN2A/B rs10811661 is a replicated T2D locus, likely affecting beta-cell cell-cycle/proliferation biology.

markers.name: IGF2BP2 intron variant
markers.description: IGF2BP2 variants are replicated T2D susceptibility loci related to beta-cell function and growth-factor signaling.

markers.name: HHEX/IDE T2D locus
markers.description: HHEX/IDE region variants are replicated T2D loci linked to pancreatic development and insulin biology.

markers.name: JAZF1 T2D locus
markers.description: JAZF1 is a replicated T2D locus with modest effects on metabolic risk.

markers.name: ADCY5 glucose locus
markers.description: ADCY5 variants are associated with fasting glucose and beta-cell insulin secretion traits.

markers.name: PROX1 fasting glucose/T2D locus
markers.description: PROX1 rs340874 is associated with fasting glucose and T2D risk in GWAS.

markers.name: WFS1 T2D locus
markers.description: WFS1 common variants influence T2D susceptibility through beta-cell stress pathways; rare WFS1 disease is separate.

markers.name: IRS1 insulin resistance locus
markers.description: IRS1 rs2943641 is linked to insulin resistance and adiposity distribution in GWAS.

markers.name: ADIPOQ -11377C>G
markers.description: ADIPOQ promoter variation can affect adiponectin levels and insulin-sensitivity context; labs and phenotype dominate.

markers.name: ADIPOQ +45T>G
markers.description: ADIPOQ rs2241766 is a candidate metabolic marker with heterogeneous association evidence.

markers.name: Q223R
markers.description: LEPR Q223R may modify leptin signaling and appetite/adiposity context, but effect is modest and non-diagnostic.

markers.name: LEP -2548G>A
markers.description: LEP promoter variation has candidate evidence for leptin levels and adiposity context. Use cautiously.

markers.name: SH2B1 obesity/insulin locus
markers.description: SH2B1 is a replicated obesity/T2D locus involved in leptin and insulin signaling.

markers.name: SEC16B BMI locus
markers.description: SEC16B is a replicated BMI/adiposity locus with small effect.

markers.name: Val66Met
markers.description: BDNF Val66Met can contextualize appetite/reward and exercise response, but it is not a weight predictor.

markers.name: Salivary amylase copy number
markers.description: AMY1 copy number can affect salivary amylase and starch digestion context. Consumer SNP files usually cannot measure it.

markers.name: APOA2 -265T>C
markers.description: APOA2 rs5082 has been studied for saturated-fat interaction with BMI. Use as diet-response research context only.

markers.name: -3826A>G
markers.description: UCP1 variation may affect thermogenesis and cold-induced energy expenditure in some contexts. Evidence is modest.

markers.name: UCP2 -866G>A
markers.description: UCP2 variation can affect mitochondrial coupling and insulin secretion context. Not diagnostic.

markers.name: E167K
markers.description: TM6SF2 E167K increases hepatic fat susceptibility while often lowering circulating lipids. Interpret with liver and lipid labs.

markers.name: MBOAT7/TMC4 liver fat locus
markers.description: MBOAT7 rs641738 is associated with fatty liver susceptibility in multiple cohorts, with modest effect.

markers.name: HSD17B13 splice/protective indel
markers.description: HSD17B13 loss-of-function/splice variation can be protective against chronic liver injury progression. It does not rule out liver disease.

markers.name: PPP1R3B liver glycogen/lipid locus
markers.description: PPP1R3B rs4841132 is associated with liver enzyme/lipid traits and hepatic metabolism context.

markers.name: SLC2A9 urate transporter variant
markers.impact: Lower uric acid / gout protection context
markers.description: SLC2A9 rs16890979 is associated with lower serum urate and reduced gout risk in many cohorts.

markers.name: Gly1057Asp
markers.description: IRS2 variation can contextualize insulin signaling and T2D susceptibility, but evidence is weaker than major GWAS loci.

markers.name: CAPN10 UCSNP-43 context
markers.description: CAPN10 was an early T2D candidate gene. Use only as low-confidence historical context.

markers.name: KLF14 metabolic locus
markers.description: KLF14 is a replicated metabolic locus affecting adipose gene regulation and insulin sensitivity traits.

markers.name: I27L common variant
markers.impact: Glycemic/lipid trait context; rare MODY gene distinction
markers.description: HNF1A common variants can modify glycemic traits, but pathogenic HNF1A variants cause MODY and require clinical sequencing.

markers.name: GLIS3 T2D/beta-cell locus
markers.description: GLIS3 is a replicated T2D and beta-cell function locus.

markers.name: E40K
markers.description: ANGPTL4 E40K is associated with lower triglycerides and altered lipoprotein lipase regulation.

markers.name: APOC3 promoter variant
markers.description: APOC3 promoter variants can affect triglyceride metabolism. Interpret with fasting triglycerides.

markers.name: Hepatic lipase -514C>T
markers.description: LIPC rs1800588 can influence hepatic lipase activity and HDL/triglyceride traits. Not a cardiovascular diagnosis.

markers.name: ATM metformin response GWAS marker
markers.description: ATM rs11212617 has been associated with metformin glycemic response in some studies. It is not a medication-selection rule.

markers.name: OCT1 metformin transporter marker
markers.description: SLC22A1/OCT1 variants can influence metformin transport and tolerability/response. Use as PGx-metabolic context only.

markers.name: OCT1 M420del
markers.impact: Reduced OCT1 transport / metformin response context
markers.description: SLC22A1 M420del can reduce OCT1 transporter function and may influence metformin response/tolerability.

markers.name: MATE1 metformin transporter marker
markers.description: SLC47A1/MATE1 variation has been studied for metformin response and renal/hepatic transport.

markers.name: OCT2 Ala270Ser
markers.description: SLC22A2/OCT2 variants can affect renal handling of metformin and other cationic drugs. Clinical utility is context-dependent.

markers.name: MODY/monogenic diabetes clinical panel
markers.description: MODY/monogenic diabetes is caused by rare pathogenic variants, not common T2D SNPs. Suspect from phenotype/family history and confirm clinically.

markers.name: Neonatal diabetes clinical panel
markers.description: Pathogenic variants in neonatal diabetes genes can change therapy, but this requires clinical genetics.

markers.name: Severe early-onset monogenic obesity panel
markers.description: Severe early-onset hyperphagic obesity can rarely be monogenic. Common obesity SNPs do not diagnose this; clinical genetics is required when phenotype fits.

markers.name: rs602662 secretor variant
markers.impact: Non-secretor status / lower serum vitamin B12 levels
markers.description: FUT2 controls the secretion of ABH blood group antigens into body fluids. Homozygous A/A results in 'non-secretor' status, which alters gut microbiome composition and is strongly linked to lower circulating serum B12 levels.

markers.name: Arg134His
markers.impact: Altered folate pathway enzymes / elevated choline requirement
markers.description: MTHFD1 rs2236225 regulates a trifunctional folate enzyme. The A (His) allele impairs folate-mediated one-carbon flow, increasing dependence on the alternative choline-dependent (BHMT) pathway in the liver.

markers.name: rs2282679 UTR variant
markers.impact: Reduced Vitamin D-binding protein / lower circulating D3
markers.description: GC encodes vitamin-D-binding protein (DBP). The C allele has been associated with lower DBP levels and modest differences in circulating total 25(OH)D in population studies; measured 25(OH)D and clinical context are more informative than this marker alone.

markers.name: rs10741657 promoter variant
markers.description: CYP2R1 is a major liver enzyme involved in converting vitamin D3 into circulating 25(OH)D. The A allele has been associated with modest differences in vitamin-D status in some studies; measured 25(OH)D, intake, sun exposure, and health context remain decisive.

markers.name: rs12785878 intron variant
markers.impact: Impaired skin synthesis of pre-vitamin D3
markers.description: DHCR7 converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol, regulating the precursor pool for Vitamin D3 synthesis in the skin. The T allele is linked to reduced efficiency in synthesizing vitamin D3 from UVB light.

markers.name: Nutrient raw-DNA non-diagnostic rule
markers.impact: Prevents nutrient deficiency/toxicity claims from genotype alone
markers.description: Nutrient-related variants can suggest altered requirements or transport/metabolism tendencies, but deficiency, toxicity, and supplementation need labs, diet context, medications, symptoms, and clinician input for high-stakes cases.

markers.name: MTHFR folic-acid overclaim guardrail
markers.description: MTHFR variants do not mean folic acid is toxic or unusable. Folate status and homocysteine are phenotype/lab questions; genotype is only context.

markers.name: Reduced folate carrier 80G>A
markers.description: SLC19A1 transports reduced folates into cells. rs1051266 may influence folate availability and homocysteine response, but effects are modest and diet-dependent.

markers.name: Serine hydroxymethyltransferase C1420T
markers.impact: Folate one-carbon partitioning / thymidylate synthesis context
markers.description: SHMT1 helps partition one-carbon units between methylation and nucleotide synthesis. The T allele is a modest folate-pathway context marker.

markers.name: Arg239Gln
markers.description: BHMT uses betaine/choline to remethylate homocysteine in the liver. rs3733890 can contextualize choline/betaine dependence but is not diagnostic.

markers.name: CBS 699C>T
markers.description: CBS variation can affect homocysteine-to-cystathionine flux in rare disease, but common SNPs like rs234706 should not be overinterpreted.

markers.name: CBS 1080C>T
markers.description: CBS rs1801181 is a common pathway marker with weak individual interpretability. Use only as context with homocysteine and sulfur-amino-acid labs.

markers.name: CBS 844ins68 insertion
markers.description: CBS 844ins68 is a structural insertion sometimes discussed in homocysteine studies. Consumer raw DNA usually does not call it reliably.

markers.name: MTHFD1L one-carbon metabolism locus
markers.description: MTHFD1L participates in mitochondrial one-carbon metabolism. Common variants are context markers for folate/homocysteine biology, not deficiency tests.

markers.name: One-carbon GWAS/context marker
markers.description: This marker can contextualize one-carbon metabolism in multi-SNP models, but has no standalone clinical interpretation.

markers.name: Cubilin B12 absorption locus
markers.description: CUBN encodes cubilin, part of the intrinsic-factor/B12 absorption system. Common variants are associated with circulating B12 levels but do not diagnose B12 deficiency.

markers.name: CUBN Ser253Phe
markers.description: CUBN coding variation can affect cubilin function. Interpret only with B12/MMA and renal context.

markers.name: Amnionless B12 absorption candidate
markers.description: AMN is part of the intestinal B12 absorption complex. Common variants are weak context markers; rare pathogenic variants require clinical diagnosis.

markers.name: Inherited B12 malabsorption clinical panel
markers.description: Rare pathogenic variants can cause severe B12 malabsorption syndromes. These are not consumer-SNP findings and need clinical genetics/lab confirmation.

markers.name: TaqI polymorphism
markers.description: VDR TaqI is commonly evaluated with BsmI/ApaI/FokI haplotypes. It may contextualize vitamin D receptor signaling but does not measure vitamin D status.

markers.name: ApaI polymorphism
markers.description: VDR ApaI contributes to common VDR haplotypes studied in bone and immune traits. Standalone effect is weak.

markers.name: Vitamin D catabolism GWAS locus
markers.impact: Altered vitamin D breakdown / circulating 25(OH)D context
markers.description: CYP24A1 helps degrade vitamin D metabolites. rs6013897 is associated with circulating vitamin D levels in GWAS but does not diagnose deficiency.

markers.name: -1260 promoter variant
markers.impact: Vitamin D activation enzyme expression candidate
markers.description: CYP27B1 converts 25(OH)D to active calcitriol. Promoter variation may modify activation context but labs dominate interpretation.

markers.name: BCMO1 beta-carotene conversion variant
markers.description: BCMO1 rs12934922 reduces conversion of beta-carotene into retinol. Carriers may rely more on preformed vitamin A if dietary retinol is low.

markers.name: BCMO1 R267S
markers.description: BCMO1 rs7501331 is a functional beta-carotene conversion marker. Use with rs12934922 and diet context.

markers.name: Beta-carotene oxygenase 2 variant
markers.description: BCO2 variation may modify carotenoid metabolism and tissue accumulation, but human nutrition interpretation is weak.

markers.name: Vitamin C transporter variant
markers.impact: Reduced vitamin C transport / lower circulating ascorbate
markers.description: SLC23A1 encodes a sodium-dependent vitamin C transporter. rs33972313 is associated with lower circulating ascorbate in population studies.

markers.name: Vitamin C transporter 2 candidate
markers.description: SLC23A2 transports vitamin C into tissues. Common variants are weak nutritional context markers and not deficiency tests.

markers.name: Val736Ala
markers.description: TMPRSS6 rs855791 affects hepcidin regulation and is associated with iron status and hemoglobin variation. It may contextualize low iron tendency.

markers.name: Transferrin GWAS marker
markers.description: TF variation influences transferrin and iron parameters. Interpret with iron labs only.

markers.name: Transferrin receptor 2 marker
markers.description: TFR2 participates in iron sensing and hepcidin regulation. Common variants are only contextual; rare pathogenic variants require clinical evaluation.

markers.name: Non-HFE hereditary iron overload panel
markers.description: Rare pathogenic variants in non-HFE iron genes can cause iron overload syndromes. Do not infer from common SNPs; confirm clinically.

markers.name: Wilson disease clinical gene panel
markers.description: Pathogenic ATP7B variants can cause Wilson disease, but consumer raw DNA is not an adequate diagnostic test.

markers.name: SEPP1/SELENOP Ala234Thr
markers.description: SELENOP transports selenium. rs3877899 has been studied for selenium status and response to supplementation.

markers.name: SEPP1/SELENOP 3UTR variant
markers.description: SELENOP rs7579 may affect selenium biomarker response. Use only with measured selenium context.

markers.name: Catalase -262C>T
markers.description: CAT promoter variation can influence catalase expression. Interpret only as antioxidant pathway context.

markers.name: GSTM1 deletion/null genotype
markers.description: GSTM1 null genotype removes GSTM1 activity and may modify response to smoke/solvent/oxidative exposures. It is not a disease result.

markers.name: GSTT1 deletion/null genotype
markers.description: GSTT1 null genotype removes GSTT1 activity and can modify exposure response. It is not diagnostic.

markers.name: FADS2 fatty-acid desaturase marker
markers.description: FADS2 variants influence PUFA desaturation and may modify response to plant-based omega-3 intake.

markers.name: FADS cluster PUFA marker
markers.description: rs1535 is a common FADS-cluster marker associated with PUFA levels. Interpret with diet and omega-3 index.

markers.name: A986S calcium-sensing receptor
markers.description: CASR rs1801725 can influence serum calcium/PTH set point. It does not diagnose calcium disorders.

markers.name: TRPM6 magnesium transporter variant
markers.description: TRPM6 participates in magnesium transport. Common variants may contextualize magnesium status but labs/symptoms dominate.

markers.name: Serum magnesium GWAS locus
markers.description: CNNM2 is a replicated serum magnesium locus. Use as context only; it does not diagnose magnesium deficiency.

markers.name: Metallothionein 1A variant
markers.description: MT1A binds metals such as zinc/copper and participates in oxidative-stress response. Common variant interpretation is low-confidence.

markers.name: Rare vitamin transporter disorder panel
markers.description: Rare pathogenic variants in vitamin transporter genes can cause serious disorders, but they require clinical genetics and are not ordinary SNP findings.

markers.name: FKBP5 intron variant
markers.impact: Altered glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity / HPA-axis stress response
markers.description: The FKBP5 rs1360780 T allele has been linked to higher FKBP5 induction and altered glucocorticoid feedback in some studies. Associations with stress sensitivity, PTSD, and depression are context-dependent and stronger in some cohorts after early-life trauma.

markers.name: A-1438G promoter
markers.description: The HTR2A A-1438G A allele has been studied for its potential to increase serotonin 2A receptor density. It is evaluated as a research-grade marker for emotional reactivity and atypical responses to serotonergic drugs.

markers.name: OXTR intron variant
markers.impact: Altered oxytocin receptor sensitivity / social stress buffering
markers.description: The OXTR rs53576 A allele is studied in relation to social-emotional traits. A-carriers (AA/AG) may experience reduced oxytocin receptor sensitivity, affecting social support seeking and stress buffering under pressure.

markers.name: MAOA coding variant
markers.impact: Lower monoamine oxidase A enzyme activity
markers.description: MAOA helps break down dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine. The rs6323 T allele has been associated with lower enzyme activity in some studies and may be linked to greater emotional reactivity under acute stress; effects vary with sex-chromosome status, environment, and context.

markers.name: Val158Met
markers.description: COMT Val158Met. Homozygous A/A (Met/Met) decreases COMT enzyme activity up to 4-fold, leading to higher prefrontal dopamine levels. Associated with high cognitive focus and executive capacity, but increases stress and anxiety vulnerability ('Worrier' type).

markers.name: TaqIA (ANKK1)
markers.description: DRD2 TaqIA (A1 allele, represented by T) is located in the adjacent ANKK1 gene and is associated with a 30-40% reduction in dopamine D2 receptor density in the striatum, potentially predisposing to reward-seeking behaviors and ADHD-like traits.

markers.name: C957T
markers.impact: Altered DRD2 mRNA stability & translation efficiency
markers.description: DRD2 C957T regulates translation efficiency and binding affinity of dopamine D2 receptors. The T allele is linked to differences in D2 receptor availability, which has been replicated in working memory and cognitive flexibility tasks.

markers.name: CNTNAP2 intron variant
markers.impact: Neurodevelopmental cell adhesion / sensory processing traits
markers.description: CNTNAP2 is involved in neural migration and synaptic development. The T allele is evaluated as a research-grade marker linked to language development variation, sensory processing, and autism spectrum traits.

markers.name: MSNP1AS variant
markers.description: MSNP1AS regulates neuronal structure. The T allele represents a minor research-level susceptibility variant replicated in broad neurodevelopmental studies, showing weak statistical correlation with autism spectrum traits.

markers.name: -1291C>G promoter
markers.impact: Altered prefrontal alpha-2A adrenergic receptor tone
markers.description: ADRA2A encodes the alpha-2A adrenergic receptor, which regulates norepinephrine in the prefrontal cortex. The G allele is linked to differences in receptor density and has been replicated in studies of methylphenidate response in ADHD.

markers.name: Pvull polymorphism
markers.description: The ESR1 Pvull G allele is a research-grade marker associated with altered transcriptional activity of estrogen receptor alpha, investigated in studies of mood fluctuations during rapid hormone drops.

markers.name: Xbal polymorphism
markers.impact: Estrogen receptor splicing / binding affinity variation
markers.description: ESR1 rs2234693 regulates receptor splicing. The T allele is evaluated as a research-grade marker linked to estrogen signaling sensitivity and emotional/physical symptoms during estrogen withdrawal.

markers.name: Progesterone receptor variant
markers.description: PGR rs8079626 A-carriers are evaluated in research regarding progesterone receptor sensitivity. Linked to mood fluctuations during the luteal progesterone spike.

markers.name: Pro129Thr
markers.impact: Increased anandamide levels / reduced FAAH expression
markers.description: FAAH degrades anandamide (the bliss molecule). The Thr129 (A) allele reduces enzyme activity, leading to elevated baseline anandamide. Associated with lower baseline anxiety, faster fear extinction, and decreased stress sensitivity.

markers.name: Asn40Asp / A118G
markers.impact: Altered mu-opioid receptor binding affinity / reward sensitivity
markers.description: The OPRM1 rs1799971 G (Asp) allele alters the mu-opioid receptor in laboratory models. Some studies report small differences in pain sensitivity or reward-related traits, but findings are inconsistent and are not diagnostic or predictive for an individual.

markers.name: -1021C>T
markers.impact: Reduced dopamine beta-hydroxylase expression / lower norepinephrine
markers.description: The DBH -1021C>T promoter T allele reduces the conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine. Homozygous T/T carriers have significantly lower plasma DBH activity, shifting dopamine-norepinephrine ratios in stress circuits.

markers.name: Neuropsych raw-DNA non-diagnostic rule
markers.impact: Prevents psychiatric/personality overcalling from common SNPs
markers.description: Single common neuropsych variants must not be used to diagnose depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, addiction, personality disorders, empathy level, intelligence, trauma response, or medication outcome. Treat common markers as weak pathway hints only.

markers.name: Major depression polygenic risk module
markers.description: Depression liability is distributed across many loci with small effects. Use only a validated PRS with ancestry/platform calibration and never as a diagnosis.

markers.name: Anxiety/stress-reactivity polygenic module
markers.description: Anxiety and stress-reactivity genetics are highly polygenic and overlap with depression, neuroticism, sleep, and trauma exposure. Use as research context only unless validated clinically.

markers.name: ADHD/attention polygenic module
markers.description: ADHD-associated common variation is polygenic. A validated PRS may contextualize attention/executive-function predisposition but cannot diagnose ADHD or predict stimulant response.

markers.name: Autism/neurodevelopmental polygenic context
markers.description: Common variants can contribute weakly to neurodevelopmental trait distributions, but autism and related traits cannot be inferred from raw SNPs. High-effect rare variants/CNVs require clinical testing.

markers.name: Rare neurodevelopmental gene panel guardrail
markers.description: Some rare pathogenic variants and CNVs have large neurodevelopmental effects, but they are not captured reliably by ordinary raw SNP files. Report only if clinically confirmed.

markers.name: 5-HTTLPR serotonin transporter promoter VNTR
markers.description: The short 5-HTTLPR allele has been studied for lower SLC6A4 transcription and stress sensitivity, but psychiatric associations are inconsistent. Treat as a pathway marker, not a mental-health result.

markers.name: 5-HTTLPR L_A/L_G modifier
markers.description: rs25531 modifies the functional interpretation of 5-HTTLPR long alleles. It is useful only as part of a correctly phased SLC6A4 promoter haplotype.

markers.name: C-1019G promoter
markers.impact: Altered serotonin 1A autoreceptor expression / mood-stress candidate
markers.description: HTR1A rs6295 G has been studied for increased autoreceptor expression and altered serotonergic feedback. Evidence is candidate-level and should remain non-diagnostic.

markers.name: HTR2A antidepressant-response candidate
markers.description: HTR2A rs7997012 appeared in antidepressant-response candidate studies but is not reliable enough for individual SSRI selection. Use only as research context.

markers.name: HTR1B G861C
markers.description: HTR1B variation has been studied for impulsivity, aggression, and substance-use traits, but effect sizes are weak and inconsistent. Keep as low-confidence pathway context.

markers.name: G-703T promoter
markers.description: TPH2 regulates brain serotonin synthesis. rs4570625 has been studied in emotional processing and amygdala-reactivity research, but is not diagnostic.

markers.name: TPH2 intronic/coding-region candidate
markers.description: TPH2 rs7305115 has appeared in candidate studies of mood and suicidality, but individual-level interpretation is not clinically valid.

markers.name: NET transporter variant
markers.description: SLC6A2 regulates norepinephrine reuptake. rs5569 has been studied for autonomic tone, attention, and antidepressant response, but evidence is not decisive.

markers.name: NET promoter variant
markers.description: SLC6A2 promoter variation can alter norepinephrine transporter expression in experimental contexts. Interpret only with autonomic/attention phenotype.

markers.name: DAT1/SLC6A3 40-bp VNTR
markers.description: The DAT1 VNTR has been studied for ADHD, reward, and stimulant response, but results are heterogeneous. Useful only if VNTR is directly genotyped.

markers.name: DAT1 3UTR SNP
markers.description: SLC6A3 rs27072 has been studied with dopamine transporter regulation and attention/reward phenotypes. Treat as weak contextual evidence.

markers.name: DRD4 exon 3 48-bp VNTR
markers.description: The DRD4 7-repeat allele has historical links to novelty seeking and ADHD-related traits, but individual prediction is weak. Direct VNTR genotyping is required.

markers.name: DRD4 -521C/T promoter
markers.description: DRD4 promoter variation may influence receptor expression, but psychiatric/behavioral associations are inconsistent and low-confidence.

markers.name: DRD2 splicing variant
markers.impact: D2 receptor isoform balance / working-memory candidate
markers.description: DRD2 rs1076560 affects D2 receptor splicing ratios in some studies and has been linked to working memory and psychosis research. Do not use diagnostically.

markers.name: DRD2 intron/splicing variant
markers.description: DRD2 rs2283265 is linked with D2 receptor isoform expression and cognitive phenotypes in research contexts. It is not diagnostic.

markers.name: Ser9Gly
markers.impact: Dopamine D3 receptor binding/limbic reward candidate
markers.description: DRD3 Ser9Gly has been studied for reward sensitivity, antipsychotic response, and movement side-effect risk. Evidence is context-dependent.

markers.name: DRD1 promoter/UTR variant
markers.description: DRD1 variants have been studied for working memory and reward learning; rs4532 should be treated as a low-confidence dopamine-pathway context marker.

markers.name: CNR1 synonymous variant
markers.description: CNR1 rs1049353 has been studied in stress response, addiction, and pain sensitivity contexts. Use only as a weak endocannabinoid pathway marker.

markers.name: CNR1 regulatory variant
markers.description: CNR1 rs2023239 has been associated with altered CB1 receptor availability and substance-response phenotypes in small studies. Not clinically actionable.

markers.name: CB2 receptor variant
markers.description: CNR2 variation may affect immune-endocannabinoid signaling, but evidence for mood or pain phenotypes is weak.

markers.name: CRHR1 intron variant
markers.description: CRHR1 variation has been studied for stress exposure interaction and depression risk. Interpretation requires environment/trauma context and remains non-diagnostic.

markers.name: CRHR1 stress-response haplotype marker
markers.description: CRHR1 rs242924 is part of stress-response haplotypes studied in trauma/depression research. Use only as haplotype context.

markers.name: CRHR1 stress-response haplotype marker
markers.description: CRHR1 rs7209436 has appeared in CRHR1 stress-buffering haplotypes. Standalone interpretation is not valid.

markers.name: BclI glucocorticoid receptor variant
markers.description: NR3C1 BclI has been studied for glucocorticoid sensitivity, stress physiology, and metabolic stress response. Interpret with phenotype/labs only.

markers.name: 9β glucocorticoid receptor variant
markers.description: NR3C1 rs6198 may affect glucocorticoid receptor beta isoform expression and stress/inflammation tone. Evidence is contextual.

markers.name: OXTR intron variant
markers.description: OXTR rs2254298 has been studied for social cognition, attachment, and stress buffering, but findings are inconsistent.

markers.name: OXTR 3UTR variant
markers.description: OXTR rs1042778 has been studied in social behavior and empathy research. Effect sizes are too weak for individual claims.

markers.name: AVPR1A RS3 microsatellite
markers.description: AVPR1A RS3 has been studied in social behavior and pair-bonding research, but direct interpretation is not clinically valid.

markers.name: AVPR1B stress-response variant
markers.description: AVPR1B variation has been explored in stress and HPA-axis regulation. Evidence remains low-confidence.

markers.name: GABRA2 synonymous/regulatory marker
markers.description: GABRA2 rs279858 has been associated with alcohol-use and impulsivity phenotypes in some cohorts. Treat as reward/GABA pathway context only.

markers.name: GAD1 promoter variant
markers.description: GAD1 encodes glutamate decarboxylase. Promoter variants have been studied in anxiety and psychosis research but are not individually reliable.

markers.name: CACNA1C intron variant
markers.impact: Voltage-gated calcium channel psychiatric GWAS locus
markers.description: CACNA1C rs1006737 is a replicated psychiatric GWAS locus, especially in bipolar/schizophrenia-spectrum research. It is a small-effect liability marker, not a diagnosis.

markers.name: ANK3 intron variant
markers.description: ANK3 is a replicated psychiatric GWAS locus related to neuronal excitability. rs10994336 should be treated as a small-effect locus-level marker only.

markers.name: ZNF804A GWAS variant
markers.description: ZNF804A rs1344706 has replicated associations in schizophrenia/bipolar research. It has no diagnostic value by itself.

markers.name: MIR137 psychiatric GWAS locus
markers.description: MIR137 rs1625579 is a schizophrenia-associated GWAS locus affecting gene-regulatory networks. It is small-effect and non-diagnostic.

markers.name: NRG1 promoter variant
markers.description: NRG1 variation has been studied in psychosis and neurodevelopmental connectivity. Evidence is mixed; keep as research context.

markers.name: Ser704Cys
markers.description: DISC1 was historically studied in psychiatric genetics, but common variant associations are not robust enough for individual interpretation.

markers.name: IL1B -511C>T promoter
markers.description: IL1B promoter variation can influence inflammatory signaling, which may interact with mood/cognition during immune activation. Not a psychiatric marker by itself.

markers.name: CRP 3UTR variant
markers.description: CRP rs1205 is associated with differences in circulating CRP levels. It may contextualize inflammation-linked fatigue/mood states but cannot diagnose inflammation.

markers.name: KIBRA memory-associated variant
markers.description: KIBRA rs17070145 has been associated with episodic memory variation in some studies. Treat as cognitive trait context only.

markers.name: Klotho KL-VS F352V component
markers.description: KL-VS haplotype markers have been studied for cognition and longevity. Interpretation requires haplotype context and is not a dementia-risk test.

markers.name: Klotho KL-VS C370S component
markers.description: rs9527025 is part of the KL-VS haplotype context. Use only with rs9536314 and do not report as standalone.

markers.name: CHRNA5 D398N
markers.description: CHRNA5 rs16969968 A is a replicated marker for heavier nicotine dependence and smoking-related risk in exposed individuals. It does not create addiction without exposure.

markers.name: CHRNA4 nicotinic receptor variant
markers.description: CHRNA4 variation has been studied for attention and nicotine response. Evidence is not sufficient for clinical interpretation.

markers.name: CHRNB2 nicotinic receptor variant
markers.description: CHRNB2 variants have been studied in nicotine dependence and attention pathways, but individual utility is weak.

markers.name: VMAT2 regulatory variant
markers.description: SLC18A2/VMAT2 controls vesicular monoamine storage. Candidate associations exist, but this should remain low-confidence pathway context.

markers.name: DOPA decarboxylase candidate
markers.description: DDC converts L-DOPA and 5-HTP into dopamine and serotonin. Common variants are not reliable predictors of neurotransmitter levels.

markers.name: Tyrosine hydroxylase Met81Val
markers.description: TH is rate-limiting for catecholamine synthesis. rs6356 has weak candidate evidence and should not be used to infer dopamine/norepinephrine levels.

markers.name: Arg16Gly
markers.description: ADRB2 Arg16Gly affects beta-adrenergic receptor regulation in some contexts and may modify stimulant/autonomic sensitivity. Evidence is not psychiatric-diagnostic.

markers.name: Gln27Glu
markers.description: ADRB2 Gln27Glu can affect receptor downregulation and autonomic response. Interpret with heart-rate/stimulant phenotype, not mood diagnosis.

markers.name: NPY promoter variant
markers.description: NPY rs16147 has been studied in stress resilience and anxiety-related phenotypes. Evidence is contextual and not diagnostic.

markers.name: COMT haplotype marker rs6269
markers.description: rs6269 contributes to COMT haplotypes that can affect enzyme expression. Use with rs4680/rs4633/rs4818 rather than standalone.

markers.name: COMT haplotype marker rs4633
markers.description: rs4633 is part of common COMT haplotypes affecting catecholamine clearance. Interpret only as haplotype context.

markers.name: COMT haplotype marker rs4818
markers.description: rs4818 is used with rs4680 and nearby SNPs to infer COMT haplotypes. It should not override phenotype.

markers.name: Asp8Asn / G22A
markers.impact: Reduced Adenosine Deaminase activity / elevated sleep pressure
markers.description: ADA breaks down adenosine (the sleep-pressure molecule). The rs73598374 A allele reduces ADA activity. A-carriers accumulate adenosine slower but have higher baseline levels, leading to deeper sleep and more slow-wave activity, but potentially higher morning sleep inertia.

markers.name: PER2 intron variant
markers.impact: Circadian rhythm phase shifting / sleep fragmentation
markers.description: PER2 is a core clock gene. The rs934945 A allele has been associated with sleep schedule disruptions, night awakenings, and anxious dreams in small clinical cohorts. A research-grade chronotype marker.

markers.name: 3111T>C
markers.impact: Altered circadian clock speed / eveningness preference
markers.description: The CLOCK 3111C allele is robustly associated with eveningness chronotype ('night owl') and elevated sleep latency. Individuals carrying the C allele may experience delayed melatonin secretion onset.

markers.name: PER3 variable number tandem repeat (4-repeat / 5-repeat)
markers.impact: Sleep homeostasis / morningness tendency / vulnerability to sleep loss
markers.description: PER3 is not a simple SNP marker. The 5-repeat VNTR has been linked with stronger homeostatic sleep pressure, earlier sleep timing in some cohorts, and larger performance/cognitive changes under sleep restriction. Useful only if the raw source includes VNTR calling or if separately genotyped.

markers.name: CRY1 c.1657+3A>C splice variant
markers.impact: Familial delayed sleep phase / prolonged circadian period
markers.description: Rare CRY1 splice-altering variant associated with delayed sleep phase patterns in families. Stronger than common chronotype SNPs when truly present, but usually absent from consumer SNP arrays.

markers.name: RGS16 chronotype GWAS lead variant
markers.description: RGS16 rs516134 is one of the replicated common chronotype markers associated with morningness. Its effect is small and should be interpreted as one point in a chronotype PRS, not as a standalone sleep identity.

markers.name: PER2 chronotype-associated variant
markers.description: PER2 is a core circadian clock gene, and multiple PER2 variants have appeared in chronotype studies. Treat this as a small-effect timing marker that belongs in a PRS or locus-level module.

markers.name: BHLHE41 p.Pro384Arg / DEC2 P384R
markers.description: Rare DEC2/BHLHE41 mutation reported in familial natural short sleep. Carriers may naturally sleep fewer hours without typical impairment, but this requires phenotype confirmation. Do not confuse with sleep deprivation tolerance from stimulants or stress.

markers.name: ADRB1 A187V
markers.impact: Familial natural short sleep / increased wakefulness
markers.description: Rare ADRB1 mutation reported in familial natural short sleepers and modeled experimentally. Use as a rare-variant flag, not a consumer-SNP score.

markers.name: NPSR1 Y206H
markers.impact: Familial natural short sleep / reduced sleep need
markers.description: Rare NPSR1 variant associated with familial natural short sleep. NPSR1 is tied to arousal signaling, so this is mechanistically plausible but should be treated as a rare family-level finding.

markers.name: GRM1 familial natural short sleep rare variants
markers.description: GRM1 rare variants have been reported in families with natural short sleep and are biologically relevant through glutamatergic signaling. Use gene-level rare-variant handling, not rsID scoring.

markers.name: SIK3 N783Y
markers.description: SIK3 N783Y has been reported as associated with human natural short sleep. This is a sleep-need regulator candidate and should be modeled as rare, high-impact when confirmed.

markers.name: ABCC9 intronic sleep-duration variant
markers.impact: Usual sleep duration / KATP-channel sleep regulation
markers.description: ABCC9 rs11046205 was reported in a GWAS of sleep duration and has biological plausibility through KATP-channel regulation. Use as a small-effect duration marker, not a determinant of sleep need.

markers.name: PAX8 locus sleep-duration GWAS variant
markers.description: The rs1823125 minor allele was associated with slightly longer usual sleep duration in CHARGE sleep-duration GWAS. The effect is minutes per allele, not hours.

markers.name: VRK2 sleep-duration GWAS locus
markers.description: VRK2 loci were identified and replicated for usual sleep duration. Use as part of a polygenic duration module rather than a single actionable marker.

markers.name: MEIS1 locus insomnia/RLS overlap variant
markers.impact: Insomnia symptoms signal with RLS/PLMS confounding
markers.description: rs113851554 has been associated with insomnia symptoms in large GWAS, but MEIS1 is also a strong restless-legs/periodic-limb movement locus. In a sleep tool, this should trigger RLS/PLMS screening before interpreting it as primary insomnia.

markers.name: HLA-DQB1*06:02 allele
markers.description: HLA-DQB1*06:02 is strongly associated with narcolepsy, especially type 1 with cataplexy, but it is not causative by itself and is common in unaffected people. Treat as a triage flag requiring phenotype and clinical sleep testing.

markers.name: T-cell receptor alpha narcolepsy-associated variant
markers.description: TCRA variants are associated with narcolepsy susceptibility and support an immune/T-cell component. Use as secondary risk context after HLA and symptoms.

markers.name: P2RY11 narcolepsy-associated variant
markers.description: P2RY11 locus has been associated with narcolepsy and may relate to immune-cell signaling. It is a small-effect immune-genetics flag, not a standalone hypersomnia marker.

markers.name: CPT1B-CHKB narcolepsy-associated variant
markers.impact: Narcolepsy susceptibility in multiple ancestry cohorts
markers.description: rs5770917 near CPT1B/CHKB has been associated with narcolepsy, originally strong in Japanese cohorts and seen in other ancestry analyses. Treat as a supporting marker only.

markers.name: MEIS1 RLS-associated variant
markers.impact: Restless legs syndrome / periodic limb movement susceptibility
markers.description: MEIS1 rs2300478 is a replicated RLS susceptibility marker. In sleep analysis, it matters because RLS/PLMS can masquerade as insomnia, fragmented sleep, hypersleep, or non-restorative sleep.

markers.name: BTBD9 RLS/PLMS-associated variant
markers.impact: Restless legs / periodic limb movement susceptibility
markers.description: BTBD9 rs3923809 is associated with RLS/PLMS in multiple studies. Add to RLS/PLMS module and screen for sleep fragmentation, leg movement, and ferritin.

markers.name: BTBD9 RLS-associated variant
markers.description: rs9296249 in BTBD9 has been associated with RLS in Asian cohorts. Use as ancestry-aware secondary evidence in an RLS module.

markers.name: MAP2K5-SKOR1 RLS-associated variant
markers.description: The MAP2K5/SKOR1 region is a replicated RLS locus; later functional work prioritizes SKOR1 regulation. Treat this as part of the RLS/PLMS risk cluster.

markers.name: PTPRD RLS/PLMS interaction variant
markers.description: PTPRD variants have been associated with RLS/PLMS and may interact with BTBD9 in some cohorts. Use as a secondary modifier, not a primary flag.

markers.name: FTO obesity/OSA-associated variant
markers.impact: OSA risk mediated largely through adiposity/body composition
markers.description: FTO rs8050136 has been associated with sleep apnea in PheWAS-type analyses, with attenuation after BMI adjustment. This is mostly an indirect body-composition pathway marker, not an airway marker.

markers.name: ERCC1/CD3EAP 3'UTR sleep-apnea symptom variant
markers.description: Rare/non-mainstream association reported for sleep-apnea symptoms. Include only as research-only until replicated in larger, clinically phenotyped cohorts.

markers.name: Obstructive sleep apnea polygenic risk score
markers.impact: Polygenic OSA liability: airway, adiposity, inflammation, craniofacial and metabolic pathways
markers.description: OSA is better represented by a PRS plus phenotype stack than by single SNPs. The MVP GWAS supports ancestry/sex heterogeneity, so scoring should use ancestry-matched weights where available.

markers.name: HLA-DQB1*05:01 allele
markers.impact: NREM parasomnia susceptibility: sleepwalking / night terrors
markers.description: HLA-DQB1*05:01 has been reported more often in sleepwalkers than controls, and sleepwalking/night terrors appear to share familial liability. Use as a parasomnia susceptibility flag only.

markers.name: Familial sleepwalking linkage locus
markers.description: A chromosome 20q12-q13.12 locus has been linked to sleepwalking in an extended family. This is not an rsID-ready consumer marker, but it belongs in a research module for familial NREM parasomnias.

markers.name: Nightmare frequency polygenic overlap module
markers.impact: Nightmare liability overlapping insomnia and psychiatric traits
markers.description: Recent GWAS work suggests nightmares have genetic overlap with insomnia and psychiatric traits, but no robust individual risk variant emerged in the 45,255-person GWAS. Use a PRS/trait-overlap module, not a single SNP.

markers.name: Serotonin transporter promoter VNTR / 5-HTTLPR
markers.impact: Dream affect / stress-related sleep disturbance candidate
markers.description: Serotonin transporter variation has candidate-level links to stress reactivity and affective sleep phenomena. Include only as a low-confidence modifier for nightmares/vivid dreams under stress, never as a direct dream marker.

markers.name: Lucid dreaming genetics gap marker
markers.impact: No robust single-SNP marker for lucid dreaming
markers.description: Lucid dreaming is sleep-related, but current evidence does not support a robust single raw-DNA marker. Track phenotype behaviorally: dream recall, REM density, sleep fragmentation, meditation/training, and cholinergic/serotonergic medication context.

markers.name: SNCA RBD GWAS locus
markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility / alpha-synucleinopathy pathway
markers.description: SNCA locus variants are associated with REM sleep behavior disorder. RBD is clinically important because dream enactment can precede Parkinsonian synucleinopathies, but genotype alone is not a diagnosis.

markers.name: GBA RBD GWAS locus
markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility / lysosomal pathway
markers.description: GBA locus variants are among the strongest RBD genetic signals. Treat as a clinically meaningful flag only when dream enactment symptoms exist.

markers.name: GBA p.Asn409Ser / N370S-tagging variant
markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder and synucleinopathy-related susceptibility
markers.description: rs76763715 is a GBA variant/locus signal associated with RBD in GWAS Catalog evidence. It should trigger careful variant interpretation, not a casual consumer-genomics claim.

markers.name: TMEM175 RBD GWAS locus
markers.description: TMEM175 was identified as an RBD risk locus in GWAS. Include as a locus-level RBD/polygenic module marker.

markers.name: INPP5F RBD GWAS locus
markers.description: INPP5F was identified as an RBD risk locus. Use as part of a PRS/locus panel, not as a standalone interpretation.

markers.name: SCARB2 RBD GWAS locus
markers.description: SCARB2 was identified as an RBD risk locus and biologically overlaps lysosomal pathways. Use as locus-level evidence in RBD module.

markers.name: Sleep bruxism candidate-gene panel
markers.impact: Sleep bruxism genetic evidence remains weak/mixed
markers.description: Sleep bruxism has reported candidate-gene studies, including serotonergic/dopaminergic genes, but evidence is mixed and not ready for consumer scoring. Keep as a research-gap panel unless a future GWAS produces robust loci.

markers.name: Sp1 binding polymorphism
markers.impact: Altered Type I collagen transcription / bone density reduction
markers.description: The COL1A1 Sp1 T-allele alters transcription factors, leading to a minor reduction in collagen Type I strength. It is replicated in studies showing reduced bone mineral density, osteopenic fracture risk, and soft-tissue injury susceptibility.

markers.name: COL5A1 3'-UTR variant
markers.impact: Altered Type V collagen mRNA stability / tendon-ligament laxity
markers.description: COL5A1 rs12722 regulates Type V collagen, which controls fibril diameter in tendons and ligaments. The T allele is linked to mechanical property variations; C/C genotypes often display higher range of motion, while T/T has been associated with tendon injury susceptibility.

markers.name: Ala531Thr
markers.impact: Type III collagen protein structure variation
markers.description: COL3A1 Ala531Thr has been investigated in relation to tissue elasticity and pelvic/mitral valve laxity. It represents a common research variant, not a pathogenic mutation, and does not indicate vascular pathology.

markers.name: GDF5 promoter variant
markers.impact: Reduced growth differentiation factor 5 expression / joint cartilage remodeling
markers.description: GDF5 is involved in joint development and cartilage repair. The T allele is associated with lower GDF5 promoter activity, showing a robust association with minor increases in osteoarthritis susceptibility (particularly knee and hip).

markers.name: 5A/6A polymorphism
markers.impact: Altered matrix metalloproteinase 3 expression / tissue remodeling
markers.description: MMP3 breaks down extracellular matrix. The 5A allele (represented by A) has higher transcription activity than 6A, altering matrix remodeling rates in tendons and ligaments. Replicated in studies of Achilles tendon injury risk.

markers.name: FBN1 intron variant
markers.impact: Fibrillin-1 structural integrity / aortic wall tension variation
markers.description: The FBN1 rs2118181 T allele is associated with increased susceptibility to sporadic thoracic aortic dissection and aneurysm in the general population, affecting baseline tissue elasticity. It is NOT diagnostic of syndromic Marfan syndrome.
