markers.name: Fibrillin-1 coding variant
markers.description: FBN1 rs8033037 is a common variant investigated in genome-wide association studies for tall stature and bone elongation in the general population. It reflects minor, non-pathogenic variation in microfibril assembly.

markers.name: R577X
markers.description: ACTN3 R577X. Homozygous T/T (X/X) is associated with little or no alpha-actinin-3 in fast muscle fibers. This may shift the performance profile toward slow-twitch endurance, but training and phenotype remain more informative than the marker alone.

markers.name: rs970547 UTR variant
markers.impact: Altered collagen XII expression / ACL injury risk
markers.description: COL12A1 rs970547 regulates Type XII collagen. The T allele is linked in association studies to altered baseline ligament properties, showing elevated susceptibility to ACL tears.

markers.name: -1562C>T
markers.impact: Altered gelatinase B expression / matrix remodeling
markers.description: MMP9 regulates gelatinase B, which cleaves collagen Type IV. The T allele increases promoter activity, modifying extracellular matrix remodeling in cardiovascular tissues and joint cartilage.

markers.name: COL1A1 promoter polymorphism
markers.impact: Altered type I collagen transcription / bone and tendon matrix modifier
markers.description: COL1A1 promoter variation can modestly influence type I collagen expression and downstream bone/tendon matrix properties. Treat as a small modifier of bone-density and tendon-resilience context, not a monogenic disorder signal.

markers.name: COL1A2 nonsynonymous matrix variant
markers.impact: Type I collagen alpha-2 chain variation / ligament and tendon stiffness modifier
markers.description: COL1A2 common variants have been studied for tendon, ligament, and bone-density traits. Evidence is inconsistent and should be treated as a weak matrix-integrity modifier only.

markers.name: COL5A1 3'-UTR / expression-linked variant
markers.impact: Type V collagen expression variation / tendon and ligament injury susceptibility
markers.description: COL5A1 regulates collagen fibril diameter. rs13946 is commonly evaluated with rs12722 as part of COL5A1 tendon-ligament susceptibility research. Effects are modest and population-dependent.

markers.name: Tenascin-C tendon matrix variant
markers.impact: Altered tendon extracellular matrix signaling / Achilles tendinopathy modifier
markers.description: TNC encodes tenascin-C, an extracellular matrix glycoprotein expressed during tendon loading and repair. rs2104772 has been investigated in Achilles tendinopathy cohorts as a common susceptibility marker.

markers.name: VEGFA +405G>C
markers.impact: Angiogenesis signaling variation / tendon and wound-healing context
markers.description: VEGFA controls angiogenesis during tendon repair and wound healing. rs2010963 may modify VEGF expression, but evidence for usable musculoskeletal prediction is weak.

markers.name: VEGFA -2578C>A promoter
markers.impact: VEGF promoter activity variation / angiogenesis and repair modifier
markers.description: The VEGFA rs699947 A allele has been studied for altered promoter activity and angiogenesis-related traits. In connective-tissue interpretation it is only a weak modifier of repair context.

markers.name: TGFB1 Pro10Leu
markers.impact: TGF-beta signaling variation / fibrosis, scarring and bone-remodeling context
markers.description: TGFB1 regulates extracellular matrix deposition, collagen synthesis, immune signaling and fibrosis. rs1800470 can be treated as a low-penetrance modifier of scarring/fibrotic tendency and bone turnover, not a diagnostic marker.

markers.name: TGFB1 Arg25Pro
markers.impact: Altered TGF-beta secretion / matrix deposition modifier
markers.description: TGFB1 rs1800471 has been studied in bone-density, fibrosis and immune-remodeling phenotypes. Use only as a weak context marker for matrix remodeling and scar behavior.

markers.name: ESR1 XbaI
markers.impact: Estrogen receptor variation / bone turnover and soft-tissue remodeling modifier
markers.description: ESR1 rs9340799 is often studied with rs2234693 for bone-density and connective-tissue phenotypes. Treat as a modest endocrine-matrix interaction marker.

markers.name: LRP5 Ala1330Val
markers.impact: Reduced WNT co-receptor signaling / lower bone mineral density susceptibility
markers.description: LRP5 participates in canonical WNT signaling, a major regulator of bone formation. rs3736228 has replicated associations with modestly lower BMD and fracture susceptibility.

markers.name: LRP5 Val667Met
markers.impact: WNT pathway variation / bone density modifier
markers.description: LRP5 rs4988321 is a common WNT-pathway variant studied in relation to bone-density traits. It may provide weak context for skeletal loading and mineralization tendency.

markers.name: WNT16 cortical bone variant
markers.impact: Altered cortical bone thickness / fracture susceptibility modifier
markers.description: WNT16 is strongly implicated in cortical bone thickness and fracture susceptibility. Common variants near WNT16 are useful as low-effect bone-strength context markers.

markers.name: WNT16 bone-density association variant
markers.impact: WNT signaling variation / cortical bone and fracture context
markers.description: rs2707466 is a WNT16-region marker studied in bone mineral density and fracture GWAS. Treat as a modest cortical-bone architecture signal.

markers.name: Sclerostin regulatory variant
markers.impact: Altered WNT inhibition / bone formation signaling modifier
markers.description: SOST encodes sclerostin, an inhibitor of bone formation. Common SOST-region variants may modestly influence BMD and bone formation signaling.

markers.name: OPG Lys3Asn
markers.impact: Osteoprotegerin signaling variation / bone resorption context
markers.description: TNFRSF11B encodes osteoprotegerin, a regulator of RANKL-mediated osteoclast activation. rs2073618 has been studied in osteoporosis, BMD and vascular calcification contexts.

markers.name: RANKL bone resorption locus
markers.impact: RANKL pathway variation / osteoclast activation context
markers.description: TNFSF11 encodes RANKL, the main osteoclast-activation signal. Common RANKL-region variants have been studied in BMD and fracture susceptibility.

markers.name: MMP1 1G/2G promoter insertion/deletion
markers.impact: Matrix metalloproteinase-1 expression variation / collagen breakdown modifier
markers.description: MMP1 initiates interstitial collagen degradation. The 2G promoter allele is associated with higher transcription in several contexts, potentially shifting matrix turnover and scar/tendon remodeling.

markers.name: MMP13 promoter variant
markers.impact: Collagenase-3 expression variation / cartilage degradation context
markers.description: MMP13 degrades type II collagen in cartilage and is biologically relevant to osteoarthritis and disc degeneration. rs2252070 has been studied as a regulatory marker.

markers.name: TIMP2 matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor variant
markers.impact: MMP inhibition balance / extracellular matrix turnover modifier
markers.description: TIMP2 inhibits matrix metalloproteinases and helps regulate collagen turnover. This marker is exploratory for connective-tissue remodeling balance.

markers.name: Elastin Ser422Gly
markers.impact: Elastin fiber structure variation / arterial and skin elasticity context
markers.description: ELN encodes elastin, central to arterial wall and skin elasticity. rs2071307 is a common coding variant studied in vascular stiffness and tissue-elasticity phenotypes.

markers.name: LOX Arg158Gln
markers.description: LOX catalyzes collagen and elastin crosslinking. rs1800449 has been studied in bone density, aortic wall integrity and extracellular matrix strength.

markers.name: DIO2 thyroid hormone activation / tendon-adjacent OA locus
markers.impact: Local thyroid hormone activation variation / osteoarthritis and cartilage context
markers.description: DIO2 affects local T3 availability in cartilage and bone. Common DIO2 variation has been studied in osteoarthritis susceptibility and cartilage metabolism, but interpretation is research-only.

markers.name: MMP8 collagenase-2 promoter variant
markers.impact: Collagen breakdown variation / periodontal and matrix remodeling context
markers.description: MMP8 degrades fibrillar collagens and is relevant to periodontal/connective tissue turnover. Common variants may influence tissue breakdown under inflammatory conditions.

markers.name: P2RX7 purinergic receptor variant
markers.description: P2RX7 participates in inflammatory signaling and bone remodeling. rs1718119 has been studied in bone-density and fracture contexts but has limited standalone utility.

markers.name: Osteopontin regulatory variant
markers.impact: Osteopontin expression variation / bone remodeling and tendon repair context
markers.description: SPP1 encodes osteopontin, involved in mineralized tissue remodeling and injury repair. Common variants are research-only connective-tissue context markers.

markers.name: Hypermobile EDS / HSD guardrail
markers.impact: No validated monogenic raw-DNA marker for most hEDS
markers.description: Hypermobile EDS remains a clinical diagnosis in the current nosology; most patients do not have a reliable validated single-gene test. A raw-DNA tool should not claim hEDS from common variants.

markers.name: Classical EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Type V/I collagen pathogenic variants / skin hyperextensibility and atrophic scarring
markers.description: Classical EDS is usually caused by pathogenic variants in COL5A1 or COL5A2, and rarely specific COL1A1 variants. Interpretation requires clinical genetic testing and phenotype correlation.

markers.name: Vascular EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Type III collagen pathogenic variants / arterial, intestinal, uterine tissue fragility
markers.description: vEDS is caused by heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in COL3A1. Because consequences can be high-stakes, any raw-DNA signal must be treated as confirmation-only.

markers.name: Kyphoscoliotic EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Collagen crosslinking/folding defects / congenital hypotonia and progressive kyphoscoliosis
markers.description: Kyphoscoliotic EDS can result from biallelic pathogenic variants in PLOD1 or FKBP14. This is a rare-disease sequencing result, not a common-SNP trait.

markers.name: Arthrochalasia EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Type I collagen exon 6 skipping / congenital hip dislocation and severe joint laxity
markers.description: Arthrochalasia EDS is associated with specific pathogenic variants affecting COL1A1 or COL1A2 processing. This requires clinical sequencing and phenotype correlation.

markers.name: Dermatosparaxis EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Procollagen N-proteinase deficiency / extreme skin fragility
markers.description: Dermatosparaxis EDS is caused by biallelic ADAMTS2 pathogenic variants affecting procollagen processing. Raw SNP arrays should not claim this condition.

markers.name: Classical-like EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Tenascin-X deficiency / hyperextensible skin without atrophic scarring
markers.description: Classical-like EDS is associated with biallelic TNXB pathogenic variants. TNXB is difficult to analyze because of pseudogene/structural complexity, so clinical testing is required.

markers.name: Cardiac-valvular EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Type I collagen alpha-2 deficiency / severe cardiac valve involvement
markers.description: Cardiac-valvular EDS is associated with biallelic COL1A2 pathogenic variants. It requires clinical genetic testing and cardiac evaluation.

markers.name: Brittle cornea syndrome gene panel
markers.impact: Corneal extracellular matrix fragility / extreme corneal thinning
markers.description: Brittle cornea syndrome is a rare recessive connective-tissue disorder mainly linked to biallelic pathogenic variants in ZNF469 or PRDM5. Clinical ophthalmologic and genetic confirmation are required.

markers.name: Spondylodysplastic EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Proteoglycan/linker-region defects / short stature and skeletal dysplasia with laxity
markers.description: Spondylodysplastic EDS is linked to biallelic pathogenic variants in B4GALT7, B3GALT6 or SLC39A13. It is not inferable from a few common SNPs.

markers.name: Musculocontractural EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Dermatan sulfate biosynthesis defect / congenital contractures and tissue fragility
markers.description: Musculocontractural EDS is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in CHST14 or DSE. This is a rare recessive diagnosis requiring clinical testing.

markers.name: Myopathic EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Type XII collagen pathogenic variants / muscle hypotonia and joint contractures/laxity
markers.description: Myopathic EDS can involve pathogenic COL12A1 variants with dominant or recessive inheritance depending on the variant. Clinical sequencing is required.

markers.name: Periodontal EDS gene panel
markers.impact: Complement pathway pathogenic variants / severe early periodontal tissue fragility
markers.description: Periodontal EDS is linked to pathogenic variants in C1R or C1S and presents with severe early-onset periodontal disease and connective-tissue findings.

markers.name: AEBP1-related EDS / classical-like EDS panel
markers.impact: Extracellular matrix organization defect / EDS-like phenotype
markers.description: Biallelic AEBP1 pathogenic variants are associated with an EDS-like connective tissue disorder. Treat as clinical sequencing only.

markers.name: FBN1-related Marfan syndrome gene panel
markers.impact: Fibrillin-1 pathogenic variants / ocular, skeletal and aortic connective-tissue syndrome
markers.description: Marfan syndrome is caused by heterozygous pathogenic FBN1 variants and diagnosed through clinical criteria plus molecular evidence. Common FBN1 SNPs are not diagnostic.

markers.name: Loeys-Dietz syndrome gene panel
markers.impact: TGF-beta pathway pathogenic variants / arterial tortuosity and aggressive aneurysm risk
markers.description: Loeys-Dietz syndrome is associated with pathogenic variants in TGF-beta pathway genes. Because vascular risk can be high even with modest dilation, interpretation must be clinical-only.

markers.name: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection gene panel
markers.impact: Aortic smooth muscle and extracellular matrix pathogenic variants / familial TAAD
markers.description: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection can be caused by rare pathogenic variants in smooth-muscle contraction and matrix genes. This is a clinical panel use-case.

markers.name: Mitral valve prolapse connective-tissue genetics panel
markers.impact: Valve extracellular matrix and developmental signaling variation
markers.description: Familial mitral valve prolapse can involve rare variants in FLNA or DCHS1, while common-variant burden contributes to sporadic disease. Echo phenotype is required.

markers.name: Osteogenesis imperfecta dominant collagen panel
markers.impact: Type I collagen pathogenic variants / bone fragility and blue sclera/dentin phenotypes
markers.description: Many OI cases are caused by pathogenic variants in COL1A1 or COL1A2. Clinical sequencing and phenotype review are required; common collagen SNPs are not diagnostic.

markers.name: Osteogenesis imperfecta recessive / collagen processing panel
markers.impact: Collagen folding, processing and mineralization defects / bone fragility
markers.description: Recessive and non-COL1A1/COL1A2 OI forms involve collagen processing and osteoblast genes. Requires clinical sequencing.

markers.name: Bruck syndrome gene panel
markers.impact: Collagen crosslinking/folding defects / bone fragility with congenital contractures
markers.description: Bruck syndrome overlaps osteogenesis imperfecta and arthrogryposis, caused by pathogenic variants in FKBP10 or PLOD2. This is clinical sequencing territory.

markers.name: Stickler syndrome gene panel
markers.impact: Type II/IX/XI collagen pathogenic variants / ocular, auditory and skeletal connective-tissue syndrome
markers.description: Stickler syndrome is genetically heterogeneous and can involve dominant or recessive collagen genes. Ocular phenotype and clinical sequencing are central.

markers.name: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia / cartilage matrix panel
markers.impact: Cartilage extracellular matrix pathogenic variants / early joint degeneration and skeletal dysplasia
markers.description: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia involves cartilage matrix genes and may present with joint pain, early osteoarthritis and skeletal changes. Diagnosis requires imaging and genetic testing.

markers.name: Cutis laxa / elastic fiber gene panel
markers.impact: Elastic fiber assembly defects / loose skin and systemic connective-tissue involvement
markers.description: Inherited cutis laxa is genetically heterogeneous and involves elastic fiber assembly or metabolism genes. Clinical exam and molecular testing are required.

markers.name: Congenital contractural arachnodactyly gene panel
markers.impact: Fibrillin-2 pathogenic variants / contractures and Marfan-like skeletal features
markers.description: Pathogenic FBN2 variants can cause congenital contractural arachnodactyly, a Marfan-overlap skeletal connective-tissue disorder. Clinical diagnosis requires molecular and physical-exam correlation.

markers.name: Marfanoid overlap / syndromic aortopathy differential panel
markers.description: Marfanoid habitus, joint laxity and aneurysm risk overlap across multiple genes. A broad clinical differential panel is preferred over consumer SNP interpretation.

markers.name: Generalized joint hypermobility polygenic module
markers.impact: Polygenic connective tissue, skeletal morphology and neuromuscular contribution to joint range
markers.description: Generalized joint hypermobility is heritable, but outside defined monogenic syndromes it is not reducible to one SNP. Treat as polygenic/contextual and confirm with physical exam.

markers.name: Osteoarthritis polygenic risk module
markers.impact: Cartilage, bone-shape, inflammation and mechanical-load susceptibility
markers.description: Osteoarthritis risk is polygenic and joint-specific. Use common variants such as GDF5/WNT/MMP pathway markers as low-effect context, not diagnosis.

markers.name: Tendon/ligament injury susceptibility polygenic module
markers.impact: Collagen fibril, matrix turnover, inflammation and biomechanics modifiers
markers.description: Tendon and ligament injury susceptibility has genetic contribution, especially collagen and MMP pathway markers, but training load and mechanics dominate real-world risk.

markers.name: Low bone density / fracture polygenic module
markers.impact: WNT, collagen, vitamin D and bone-resorption pathway aggregate risk
markers.description: Bone mineral density and fracture risk are heritable and polygenic. Use PRS as context only; DEXA and fracture history are the phenotype anchors.

markers.name: Idiopathic scoliosis / spinal alignment polygenic module
markers.impact: Spinal growth and connective-tissue architecture susceptibility
markers.description: Idiopathic scoliosis has heritable components and GWAS loci, but raw DNA is not clinically predictive. Use only as background context for spine phenotype.

markers.name: Hernia / pelvic organ prolapse connective-tissue module
markers.impact: Fascial collagen composition and pelvic/abdominal wall connective-tissue susceptibility
markers.description: Hernia and pelvic organ prolapse have heritable connective-tissue components, but risk is polygenic and heavily modified by mechanical pressure, childbirth history, obesity, cough and surgery.

markers.name: Varicose veins / venous wall polygenic module
markers.impact: Venous valve, smooth muscle and extracellular matrix susceptibility
markers.description: Varicose veins have substantial heritability and replicated GWAS loci, but phenotype depends on venous anatomy, standing time, age, pregnancy history and BMI.

markers.name: Keloid / hypertrophic scar polygenic module
markers.impact: Fibroblast activation, TGF-beta signaling and ancestry-linked scar response
markers.description: Keloid and hypertrophic scarring are genetically influenced and ancestry-dependent. Use as context only; personal scar history is more predictive than raw DNA.

markers.name: Striae/stretch-mark and skin elasticity module
markers.impact: Elastic fiber, collagen remodeling and hormonal-growth context
markers.description: Stretch marks and skin elasticity are heritable but strongly influenced by rapid growth, weight change, corticosteroid exposure and hormones. Interpret only as a low-confidence elasticity context module.

markers.name: Intervertebral disc degeneration polygenic module
markers.impact: Cartilage matrix, inflammation and mechanical-loading susceptibility
markers.description: Disc degeneration has genetic and mechanical components, including collagen, aggrecan, inflammatory and MMP pathways. Raw DNA should not be used diagnostically.

markers.name: Common collagen SNPs are not EDS diagnostic
markers.impact: Prevents false EDS/Marfan/OI calls from benign common variants
markers.description: Common variants in COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, COL5A1, COL5A2, FBN1, MMP and GDF5 can modify traits but should never be labeled as EDS/Marfan/OI unless clinically classified pathogenic/likely pathogenic.

markers.name: Negative raw DNA does not rule out connective tissue disease
markers.impact: Prevents false reassurance from missing rare variants, CNVs and untested genes
markers.description: A negative consumer raw-DNA scan does not rule out EDS, Marfan, LDS, OI, Stickler, aortopathy or other heritable connective-tissue disorders.

markers.name: Variant of uncertain significance is not actionable
markers.impact: Prevents over-interpretation of uncertain connective-tissue variants
markers.description: A VUS in a connective-tissue gene is not a diagnosis and should not guide high-stakes medical or surgical decisions without reclassification and phenotype correlation.

markers.name: Connective-tissue red flags override SNP interpretation
markers.impact: Phenotype-first escalation rule for high-risk tissue fragility signs
markers.description: Certain findings require medical evaluation regardless of raw DNA: arterial aneurysm/dissection history, lens dislocation, spontaneous organ rupture, recurrent major dislocations, severe skin fragility, blue sclera with fractures, retinal detachment, or family history of sudden aortic death.

markers.name: Raw DNA is not sports or injury clearance
markers.impact: Prevents training/sports decisions from being based on marker scans
markers.description: Tendon, ligament, bone-density and aortopathy markers should not be used to clear high-load sports, aggressive stretching, heavy lifting or contact sports when symptoms or clinical red flags exist.

markers.name: PRS transferability limitation for connective-tissue traits
markers.impact: Prevents overconfidence from European-biased GWAS/polygenic scores
markers.description: Most connective-tissue PRS models are not uniformly portable across ancestries. Use PRS as research context unless validated for the user's ancestry and target phenotype.

markers.name: Thr17Ala
markers.impact: Altered T-cell activation regulation / autoimmune susceptibility
markers.description: CTLA-4 is an immune checkpoint receptor. The G (Ala) allele reduces CTLA-4 cell surface expression, leading to elevated T-cell activation and increased baseline predisposition to autoimmune conditions including thyroiditis.

markers.name: -1C>T
markers.impact: Altered CD40 translation / thyroid antibody production
markers.description: The C allele of the CD40 -1C>T translation start site variant increases translation efficiency, promoting B-cell activation and elevating baseline levels of thyroid antibodies in susceptible individuals.

markers.name: TSHR intron variant
markers.impact: Altered thyroid stimulating hormone receptor expression
markers.description: The TSHR rs179247 A allele is a replicated risk modifier associated with autoimmune thyroid diseases (such as Graves' disease and Hashimoto's), affecting receptor signaling sensitivity.

markers.name: rs2235544 intron variant
markers.description: DIO1 contributes to peripheral deiodination. The C allele has been linked to small shifts in Free T4/Free T3 ratios in some studies, reflecting a possible difference in conversion context rather than a thyroid diagnosis.

markers.name: Thyroid raw-DNA non-diagnostic rule
markers.impact: Prevents overcalling thyroid disease from common SNPs
markers.description: Common thyroid-function and thyroid-autoimmune SNPs are hypothesis flags only. Thyroid status is determined by labs, symptoms, antibody testing, medication status, iodine/selenium/iron status, pregnancy/postpartum context, and clinician evaluation.

markers.name: PMDD-thyroid-hormone overlay guardrail
markers.impact: Prevents confusing thyroid dysfunction, PMS, and PMDD
markers.description: PMDD is primarily a cyclic luteal-phase mood disorder involving abnormal sensitivity to normal ovarian steroid fluctuations, especially progesterone/allopregnanolone and estrogen response. Thyroid dysfunction or autoimmunity can worsen fatigue, mood, anxiety, bleeding, and cycle symptoms, but thyroid genetics cannot diagnose PMDD.

markers.name: Autoimmune thyroid polygenic/environment interaction rule
markers.description: Autoimmune thyroid disease reflects immune genetics plus environmental triggers such as iodine shifts, postpartum immune rebound, infections, smoking, selenium status, vitamin D status, stress physiology, and gut/immune context. Single SNPs should not be interpreted deterministically.

markers.name: Autoimmune thyroid disease polygenic susceptibility panel
markers.impact: Polygenic susceptibility to Hashimoto/Graves-spectrum thyroid autoimmunity
markers.description: Autoimmune thyroid disease has a polygenic architecture involving HLA class II, immune checkpoint, cytokine, B-cell, and thyroid-antigen pathways. Use only as a population-calibrated risk module, never as a diagnosis.

markers.name: Hashimoto thyroiditis clinical-confirmation overlay
markers.impact: Autoimmune hypothyroid tendency / thyroid antibody confirmation pathway
markers.description: Hashimoto thyroiditis is confirmed with thyroid antibodies, thyroid function labs, ultrasound when needed, and clinical course. Genetic variants can support susceptibility hypotheses but cannot determine active autoimmune thyroid destruction.

markers.name: Graves disease clinical-confirmation overlay
markers.impact: Autoimmune hyperthyroid tendency / TRAb-TSI confirmation pathway
markers.description: Graves disease is a thyroid-stimulating antibody condition. Genetics can flag immune susceptibility, but diagnosis requires hyperthyroid labs and TSH receptor antibody testing.

markers.name: HLA class II autoimmune thyroid susceptibility panel
markers.impact: Immune antigen-presentation susceptibility for autoimmune thyroid disease
markers.description: HLA class II haplotypes contribute substantially to autoimmune thyroid disease susceptibility through antigen presentation. HLA typing is haplotype-based and is not reliably inferred from a few rsIDs.

markers.name: TSH/Free T4/Free T3 thyroid function polygenic panel
markers.impact: Common genetic variation affecting thyroid hormone set point
markers.description: Normal-range TSH and FT4 variation is polygenic. A thyroid-function PRS may help explain a person's baseline set point, but it cannot diagnose hypo- or hyperthyroidism.

markers.name: Congenital thyroid dysgenesis gene panel
markers.description: Pathogenic variants in thyroid development genes can cause congenital hypothyroidism or syndromic thyroid dysfunction. This is a clinical sequencing domain, not a consumer-SNP interpretation.

markers.name: Thyroid hormone synthesis/dyshormonogenesis gene panel
markers.description: Rare pathogenic variants in iodine transport, organification, thyroglobulin, thyroid peroxidase, or dual oxidase pathways can impair thyroid hormone synthesis. Interpret only from clinical sequencing and phenotype.

markers.name: Thyroid hormone resistance/transport/metabolism panel
markers.description: Rare pathogenic variants can cause thyroid hormone resistance, transporter defects, or abnormal selenium-dependent thyroid hormone metabolism. These patterns require specialist interpretation because labs may look paradoxical.

markers.name: Selenium-dependent thyroid antioxidant defense panel
markers.impact: Thyroid oxidative-stress buffering and deiodinase cofactor demand
markers.description: The thyroid produces hydrogen peroxide during hormone synthesis and depends heavily on selenium-dependent antioxidant systems and deiodinases. This pathway is useful for hypothesis generation but should be confirmed with diet/labs.

markers.name: Thyroid nodule/cancer non-inference rule
markers.impact: Prevents tumor or nodule claims from thyroid-function genetics
markers.description: Common thyroid-function or autoimmune SNPs must not be used to infer thyroid nodules, thyroid cancer, tumor mutation status, or need for biopsy. Germline risk and tumor somatic biomarkers answer different questions.

markers.name: PDE8B intron variant
markers.impact: Higher genetically influenced TSH set point
markers.description: PDE8B regulates cAMP signaling downstream of the TSH receptor. The A allele is associated with a small increase in circulating TSH in population studies.

markers.name: FOXE1 region thyroid-function variant
markers.impact: Thyroid development/function locus; TSH/hypothyroidism association context
markers.description: FOXE1 is a thyroid-development transcription factor. The rs965513 A allele tags a thyroid-function locus associated in studies with thyroid traits and hypothyroidism/cancer-related phenotypes, but it is not clinically interpretable by itself.

markers.name: CAPZB upstream TSH locus
markers.description: This locus upstream of CAPZB has been associated with population variation in TSH. It should be interpreted as a small-effect thyroid set-point marker.

markers.name: CAPZB-region thyroid-function marker
markers.description: CAPZB-region variants have been reported in thyroid-function association studies. Use as a weak TSH set-point modifier only.

markers.name: CTLA4 CT60 variant
markers.impact: Altered immune checkpoint signaling / autoimmune thyroid susceptibility
markers.description: CTLA4 CT60 has been associated with autoimmune thyroid disease in multiple cohorts. It is an immune-susceptibility marker, not evidence of active thyroid autoimmunity.

markers.name: CTLA4 promoter -318C>T
markers.description: The CTLA4 -318T allele has been studied for altered immune checkpoint expression and autoimmune thyroid susceptibility. Treat as research-only unless replicated in the target ancestry.

markers.name: IL2RA/CD25 intron variant
markers.description: IL2RA/CD25 contributes to regulatory T-cell biology and appears across autoimmune disease studies. In thyroid contexts, treat it as an autoimmune-clustering marker.

markers.name: IL2RA autoimmune-risk locus
markers.description: IL2RA variants may contribute to autoimmune disease overlap. Use as a broad immune susceptibility marker, not a thyroid-specific finding.

markers.name: IL21 autoimmune thyroid candidate variant
markers.description: IL21 is a cytokine locus implicated in immune activation and some autoimmune thyroid studies, especially Graves disease susceptibility. Treat as research-only.

markers.name: FOXP3 promoter variant
markers.impact: Regulatory T-cell transcription factor variation / autoimmune tolerance context
markers.description: FOXP3 controls regulatory T-cell function. The promoter A allele has been investigated in autoimmune disease and thyroid autoimmunity cohorts, but it is not clinically actionable from raw DNA.

markers.name: FCRL3 promoter variant
markers.description: FCRL3 is involved in B-cell regulation and autoantibody-prone immune states. Use as a research-level autoimmune-thyroid overlap marker.

markers.name: IFIH1/MDA5 Ala946Thr
markers.impact: Innate antiviral immune sensing / autoimmune clustering
markers.description: IFIH1 affects viral RNA sensing and is linked to autoimmune clustering, especially type 1 diabetes and related autoimmunity. It can be used as a broad autoimmune-context marker for thyroid autoimmunity.

markers.name: STAT4 intron variant
markers.description: STAT4 is a shared autoimmune susceptibility locus involved in cytokine signaling. Use only as a general immune-inflammatory context marker.

markers.name: IL10 -592C>A promoter variant
markers.description: IL10 promoter variants may shift anti-inflammatory cytokine tone and have been examined across autoimmune conditions. Use only as weak immune-modulation context.

markers.name: IL10 -1082A>G promoter variant
markers.description: IL10 -1082G has been studied for altered IL-10 production and autoimmune susceptibility. This is a low-confidence modifier.

markers.name: IL1B +3954C>T
markers.impact: Inflammasome cytokine tone / inflammatory symptom context
markers.description: IL1B variants have been studied across inflammatory and autoimmune phenotypes. In thyroid interpretation, this is only a general inflammatory reactivity overlay.

markers.name: IL2 -330T>G promoter variant
markers.impact: T-cell growth cytokine signaling / autoimmune context
markers.description: IL2 supports T-cell proliferation and regulatory immune balance. Common variants are weak autoimmune-context markers, not thyroid-specific findings.

markers.name: PMDD ovarian-steroid sensitivity research overlay
markers.description: PMDD-relevant biology is better described as abnormal cellular and CNS response to normal ovarian steroid changes, not abnormal hormone levels. This panel is a research overlay and should not drive scoring without prospective symptom tracking.

markers.name: ESC/E(Z) ovarian-steroid cellular response panel
markers.impact: PMDD-associated cellular response pathway, not SNP-scored
markers.description: Cell-line studies suggest PMDD may involve altered ESC/E(Z) complex expression and response to estradiol/progesterone. This is not currently a consumer-DNA scoring module.

markers.name: Allopregnanolone/GABA-A PMDD sensitivity panel
markers.description: Allopregnanolone modulation of GABA-A receptors is a leading PMDD mechanism. Current evidence supports biology-level interpretation, not individual raw-DNA prediction.

markers.name: PGR PROGINS / Val660Leu component
markers.impact: Progesterone receptor signaling context / luteal symptom overlay
markers.description: PGR PROGINS-related variation has been studied in reproductive hormone sensitivity. It is included as a weak luteal-phase symptom overlay, not as a PMDD marker.

markers.name: Postpartum thyroiditis susceptibility overlay
markers.description: Postpartum thyroiditis risk is driven by thyroid autoantibody status and immune rebound after pregnancy. Genetic autoimmune susceptibility can provide context, but antibodies and timing are decisive.

markers.name: Celiac-thyroid autoimmune clustering panel
markers.impact: Shared autoimmune clustering affecting thyroid and gut/nutrient status
markers.description: Celiac disease and autoimmune thyroid disease cluster partly through HLA and immune genetics. This matters because malabsorption can affect thyroid medication, iron, B12, folate, and mood symptoms.

markers.name: Type 1 diabetes-thyroid autoimmune cluster panel
markers.description: Autoimmune thyroid disease commonly clusters with type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune endocrinopathies. Use this as a context flag for lab review when symptoms or family history fit.

markers.name: Thyroid hormone replacement response context panel
markers.impact: Hypothesis layer for persistent symptoms on thyroid replacement
markers.description: DIO2/DIO1 and transport/metabolism biology can be used to contextualize persistent symptoms on levothyroxine, but medication changes require labs and clinician management.

markers.name: Iodine-status thyroid response context
markers.impact: Iodine-sensitive thyroid hormone synthesis and autoimmunity context
markers.description: Iodine deficiency and excess can both affect thyroid function and autoimmunity. Genetic thyroid synthesis pathways can add context, but iodine recommendations require diet/lab/geography context.

markers.name: Iron/B12/folate thyroid-symptom mimic overlay
markers.impact: Fatigue/brain fog/mood overlap with thyroid symptoms
markers.description: Iron, B12, folate, and methylation-related findings can mimic or worsen thyroid-like symptoms. This overlay belongs across nutrients and thyroid interpretation.

markers.name: Vitamin D-thyroid autoimmune context panel
markers.impact: Vitamin D signaling and autoimmune thyroid context
markers.description: Vitamin D pathway variants can contextualize immune tone, but thyroid antibody status and actual 25(OH)D levels are more informative than genotype.

markers.name: Estrogen-thyroid binding context panel
markers.impact: Estrogen effects on thyroid-binding globulin and symptom interpretation
markers.description: Estrogen status can change thyroid-binding globulin and total thyroid hormone levels. This matters for cycle, pregnancy, oral estrogen, and hormone therapy interpretation but is not a genotype-only trait.

markers.name: Stress-HPA-thyroid conversion context panel
markers.impact: Stress/cortisol effects on deiodination and thyroid-like symptoms
markers.description: Stress physiology can alter perceived thyroid symptoms and peripheral thyroid hormone conversion. This is a cross-domain context panel, not a thyroid diagnosis module.

markers.name: GPX4 3'-UTR selenium-response variant
markers.description: GPX4 is a selenium-dependent antioxidant enzyme. This variant has been studied for selenium response and oxidative stress; in thyroid interpretation it is a low-confidence antioxidant-context marker.

markers.name: SELENOS promoter variant
markers.description: SELENOS participates in endoplasmic-reticulum stress and inflammatory response. Include only as a research-level selenium/inflammation overlay.

markers.name: DUOX2 common variant context
markers.description: DUOX2 supports thyroid hormone synthesis by generating hydrogen peroxide for TPO-mediated iodination. Common variants should be treated as low-confidence context; rare pathogenic variants require sequencing.

markers.name: SLC5A5/NIS iodine transport context marker
markers.description: SLC5A5 encodes the sodium-iodide symporter. Common markers are not diagnostic; pathogenic transport defects are a clinical genetics issue.

markers.name: Thyroglobulin autoimmune-thyroid candidate marker
markers.description: TG encodes thyroglobulin, a major thyroid autoantigen. Common TG variants have been studied in autoimmune thyroid disease, but antibody testing is the actual phenotype.

markers.name: Thyroglobulin candidate variant
markers.description: This TG-region marker is included only as research-level autoimmune thyroid context.

markers.name: Thyroid peroxidase candidate marker
markers.description: TPO is both a thyroid hormone synthesis enzyme and major autoantigen. Common variants are weak; anti-TPO antibodies are the clinically relevant phenotype.

markers.name: TPO candidate autoimmune/synthesis marker
markers.description: TPO-region variation can be used only as thyroid autoantigen/synthesis pathway context.

markers.name: GCKR metabolic-thyroid bridge marker
markers.impact: Metabolic-liver substrate partitioning / thyroid symptom overlap
markers.description: GCKR affects glucose-triglyceride partitioning and can contribute to metabolic symptoms that overlap with thyroid complaints. It is included as a metabolic-thyroid bridge, not a thyroid locus.

markers.name: APOE e4 marker
markers.impact: APOE e4 isoform structural driver / LDL cholesterol elevations
markers.description: APOE rs429358 C is one of the two alleles used to assign an APOE e2/e3/e4 haplotype; rs7412 must be interpreted with it. An e4 haplotype is associated with higher LDL cholesterol and higher cardiovascular and late-onset Alzheimer’s disease risk in population studies, with effects varying by copy number, ancestry, age, and other factors.

markers.name: APOE e2/e3/e4 marker
markers.impact: APOE isoform determination (e2, e3, e4 haplotype)
markers.description: rs7412 is the second allele used with rs429358 to assign the APOE e2/e3/e4 haplotype. T/T at rs7412 with T/T at rs429358 is consistent with e2/e2, which is often associated with lower LDL but can increase Type III hyperlipoproteinemia susceptibility; G/G at rs7412 with C/C at rs429358 is consistent with e4/e4. Confirm the haplotype clinically before acting on it.

markers.name: Heart Attack Gene marker
markers.impact: Altered cell cycle regulation in vascular walls
markers.description: The 9p21 non-coding region regulates vascular smooth muscle. The rs10757278 G allele is one of the most replicated risk markers for early-onset coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction, independent of lipid levels.

markers.name: Glu298Asp
markers.impact: Altered nitric oxide synthesis / vascular recovery
markers.description: NOS3 synthesizes nitric oxide, which regulates vasodilation and blood flow. The T (Asp) allele reduces enzyme function, potentially impairing endothelial nitric oxide production, athletic recovery, and arterial dilation under stress.

markers.name: -786T>C promoter
markers.impact: Reduced nitric oxide synthase promoter transcription
markers.description: The C allele of rs2070744 is located in the NOS3 promoter, decreasing transcription rate. Associated with reduced basal nitric oxide production. Works synergistically with rs1799983 to affect vascular tone.

markers.name: R46L loss-of-function marker
markers.impact: Reduced PCSK9 activity / lower LDL cholesterol / lower CAD risk
markers.description: The PCSK9 rs11591147 T allele encodes the R46L loss-of-function variant. Carriers tend to have lower LDL-C and lower coronary disease risk, modeling the biology targeted by PCSK9 inhibitors.

markers.name: LDLR intronic LDL-lowering marker
markers.impact: Increased LDL receptor pathway efficiency / lower LDL cholesterol
markers.description: The LDLR rs6511720 T allele has been repeatedly associated with lower LDL-C. It is a common regulatory-marker proxy, not the same thing as a pathogenic familial hypercholesterolemia variant.

markers.name: 1p13.3 LDL cholesterol locus
markers.impact: Altered hepatic VLDL/LDL handling / lower LDL cholesterol tendency
markers.description: The rs599839 G allele at the CELSR2-PSRC1-SORT1 locus has been associated with lower LDL-C and lower atherosclerotic burden in several cohorts. The locus is mechanistically linked to hepatic sortilin regulation of lipoprotein secretion.

markers.name: HMG-CoA reductase lipid and statin-target marker
markers.impact: Lower LDL cholesterol tendency through HMGCR pathway modulation
markers.description: The HMGCR rs12916 T allele tags reduced HMGCR activity and lower LDL-C in many datasets. It is useful as a biology-of-statin-target marker, but its effect is small and not a statin-response substitute.

markers.name: APOC3 loss-of-function triglyceride protection panel
markers.impact: Reduced ApoC-III activity / lower triglycerides / lower CAD risk
markers.description: Rare loss-of-function variants in APOC3 lower triglycerides and have been associated with lower coronary disease risk. This is a gene-level screen, not a single consumer SNP marker.

markers.name: LDL-C polygenic score module
markers.impact: Polygenic LDL cholesterol burden / lifelong ApoB exposure tendency
markers.description: LDL-C is strongly polygenic. Use this module to aggregate many small-effect alleles across LDL receptor, ApoB production, intestinal sterol absorption, hepatic secretion, and statin-target pathways. The output should be a percentile or burden estimate, never a diagnosis.

markers.name: Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein polygenic module
markers.impact: Polygenic triglyceride and remnant-cholesterol handling tendency
markers.description: Triglyceride levels reflect both polygenic lipoprotein handling and metabolic state. Aggregate TG-risk variants across APOA5, LPL, APOC3, ANGPTL4, GCKR, MLXIPL, and TRIB1 rather than over-weighting any single SNP.

markers.name: HDL-C genetics guardrail module
markers.impact: HDL-C level genetics / HDL function uncertainty
markers.description: HDL-C-associated variants can change measured HDL-C without proving improved reverse cholesterol transport or lower event risk. This module should report HDL-C genetic tendency but explicitly avoid claiming cardiovascular protection from high HDL alone.

markers.name: Coronary artery disease polygenic score module
markers.impact: Genome-wide CAD susceptibility / atherosclerosis burden tendency
markers.description: CAD risk is polygenic and pathway-diverse: lipid biology, vascular wall remodeling, inflammation, thrombosis, blood pressure, and smooth-muscle behavior. A PRS module is more honest than single-SNP scoring for most people.

markers.name: Familial hypercholesterolemia core gene panel
markers.impact: Monogenic lifelong LDL-C elevation / premature ASCVD risk
markers.description: Pathogenic variants in LDLR, APOB, PCSK9, and LDLRAP1 can cause familial hypercholesterolemia or related severe LDL-C phenotypes. This is clinically actionable, but raw SNP files are inadequate for ruling it in or out.

markers.name: LDLR pathogenic variant / CNV panel
markers.impact: Reduced or absent LDL receptor function / high LDL-C from birth
markers.description: LDLR pathogenic variants are among the common monogenic causes of familial hypercholesterolemia. Variant interpretation requires ACMG/ClinGen-grade curation plus lipid phenotype.

markers.name: Familial defective ApoB / APOB pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Impaired LDL particle binding to LDL receptor / high LDL-C
markers.description: Pathogenic APOB gain-of-function/binding-domain variants can produce familial defective ApoB, clinically resembling FH with elevated LDL-C and premature ASCVD risk.

markers.name: PCSK9 gain/loss-of-function clinical lipid panel
markers.impact: LDL receptor degradation pathway modulation / LDL-C high or low
markers.description: PCSK9 gain-of-function variants can cause high LDL-C/FH-like phenotypes, while loss-of-function variants lower LDL-C and CAD risk. Direction depends on the specific variant.

markers.name: TCF21 coronary artery disease locus
markers.impact: Vascular smooth muscle / fibroblast lineage remodeling signal
markers.description: TCF21 rs12190287 is a replicated CAD locus marker pointing toward vascular wall remodeling rather than lipid levels alone. Useful as a CAD-pathway marker in PRS context.

markers.name: PHACTR1/EDN1 vascular disease locus
markers.impact: Vascular tone/remodeling / CAD, migraine, SCAD/FMD pleiotropy signal
markers.description: PHACTR1 rs9349379 is a pleiotropic vascular locus associated with coronary artery disease and other arterial phenotypes. It is useful but direction and phenotype context can differ by disease.

markers.name: MRAS CAD susceptibility marker
markers.impact: Ras signaling / coronary artery disease susceptibility
markers.description: MRAS rs9818870 is a replicated CAD GWAS marker. Its value is primarily as part of a CAD PRS, not as a standalone interpretation.

markers.name: CXCL12 coronary artery disease locus
markers.impact: Chemokine signaling / vascular repair and CAD susceptibility
markers.description: CXCL12 rs501120 is a replicated CAD-associated locus with immune/vascular repair biology. It belongs in PRS or pathway interpretation, not standalone risk calling.

markers.name: ABO non-O thrombotic/coronary marker
markers.impact: Higher von Willebrand factor / thrombosis and CAD tendency by ABO biology
markers.description: ABO locus variants influence circulating von Willebrand factor and factor VIII. Non-O blood-group genetics can modestly affect thrombotic and coronary risk, but ABO tagging from raw SNPs can be ambiguous.

markers.name: Blood pressure polygenic score module
markers.description: Blood pressure genetics is highly polygenic, with many small-effect loci affecting kidney sodium handling, vascular tone, endocrine signaling, and smooth muscle calcium handling. Use PRS-style scoring, not single-SNP diagnosis.

markers.name: 10q24 blood pressure marker
markers.impact: CYP17A1/NT5C2 blood-pressure association locus / steroidogenesis signal
markers.description: The rs11191548 C allele near CYP17A1/NT5C2 is a replicated blood-pressure locus marker, but direction and phenotype details vary across cohorts. Use as a BP-pathway/PRS input rather than a standalone hypertension risk call.

markers.name: ATP2B1 blood pressure marker
markers.impact: ATP2B1 blood-pressure association marker / vascular smooth muscle calcium-handling biology
markers.description: ATP2B1 rs2681472 sits in a replicated blood-pressure locus affecting calcium transport biology. Published direction can vary by ancestry, LD structure, and phenotype definition, so this should be used as a locus/pathway marker or PRS input rather than a standalone risk-allele call.

markers.name: UMOD renal salt-handling blood pressure marker
markers.impact: UMOD renal salt-handling association marker / context-dependent BP and renal signal
markers.description: UMOD rs13333226 tags renal uromodulin/salt-handling biology. Some cohorts associate the G allele with lower hypertension risk and lower urinary uromodulin, while others report context-specific BP differences. Treat as a renal salt-handling marker, not a simple risk allele.

markers.name: Angiotensinogen M235T salt/BP marker
markers.impact: Renin-angiotensin system / salt-sensitive blood pressure hypothesis
markers.description: AGT rs699 C allele has been associated with angiotensinogen levels and hypertension in some studies, but results are population- and environment-dependent. Treat as a low-confidence salt/BP hypothesis marker.

markers.name: Factor V Leiden / Arg506Gln
markers.impact: Activated protein C resistance / increased venous thromboembolism risk
markers.description: F5 rs6025 A is Factor V Leiden, one of the most established inherited thrombophilia variants. It increases venous clot risk, especially with estrogen exposure, surgery, immobility, pregnancy/postpartum, smoking, obesity, or prior VTE.

markers.name: Prothrombin G20210A
markers.impact: Higher prothrombin levels / increased venous thromboembolism risk
markers.description: F2 rs1799963 A is the prothrombin G20210A variant, a well-established inherited thrombophilia marker. It is weaker than many monogenic disorders but clinically relevant in VTE risk contexts.

markers.name: PAI-1 4G/5G promoter marker
markers.impact: Higher PAI-1 expression / hypofibrinolysis tendency hypothesis
markers.description: The SERPINE1 4G allele is associated with higher PAI-1 expression in many studies, potentially reducing fibrinolysis. Evidence for clinical thrombosis prediction is inconsistent, so use only as a research-grade clotting/fibrinolysis tendency marker.

markers.name: Venous thromboembolism polygenic and thrombophilia module
markers.impact: Polygenic clotting burden / venous thrombosis susceptibility
markers.description: VTE genetics combines a few high-impact common variants, especially F5 Leiden and F2 G20210A, with many smaller-effect clotting, fibrinolysis, and ABO-related variants. Report as risk-context, not diagnosis.

markers.name: Atrial fibrillation polygenic score module
markers.description: Atrial fibrillation has a strong polygenic component involving atrial development, ion channels, conduction, and structural remodeling. Single SNPs are weak; a PRS module plus ECG/history is the correct framing.

markers.name: 4q25 atrial fibrillation marker
markers.description: PITX2/4q25 rs2200733 T is one of the most replicated atrial fibrillation risk alleles. It should be used as an AF susceptibility flag, not a rhythm diagnosis.

markers.name: ZFHX3 atrial fibrillation marker
markers.description: ZFHX3 rs2106261 T is a replicated AF-associated marker. It has no standalone diagnostic meaning but is useful in AF PRS/pathway interpretation.

markers.name: KCNN3 atrial fibrillation marker
markers.impact: Calcium-activated potassium channel biology / AF susceptibility
markers.description: KCNN3 rs13376333 T is associated with AF risk in multiple studies and points toward potassium-channel/atrial repolarization biology.

markers.name: SCN10A conduction / PR interval marker
markers.impact: Cardiac conduction interval variation / PR and QRS trait signal
markers.description: SCN10A rs6795970 is associated with cardiac conduction traits such as PR interval and QRS duration. It can flag conduction biology, but not arrhythmia diagnosis.

markers.name: QT interval marker
markers.impact: QT interval prolongation susceptibility / repolarization biology
markers.description: NOS1AP rs10494366 T is associated with longer QT interval in population studies. It is useful for drug-QT caution context, not for diagnosing congenital long QT syndrome.

markers.name: PR/QRS/QT interval genetics module
markers.impact: Polygenic cardiac conduction and repolarization timing
markers.description: ECG intervals are heritable and polygenic. Use this module to annotate PR, QRS, and QT trait tendencies, especially when reviewing arrhythmia susceptibility and medication-QT context.

markers.name: Long QT syndrome clinical gene panel
markers.impact: Congenital repolarization disorder / syncope and malignant arrhythmia susceptibility
markers.description: Pathogenic variants in KCNQ1, KCNH2, and SCN5A account for most molecularly explained congenital long QT syndrome, with additional high-impact rare genes. This belongs in a clinical sequencing track, not raw SNP scoring.

markers.name: Brugada syndrome SCN5A clinical panel
markers.description: SCN5A is currently the best-supported Brugada syndrome gene under ClinGen-style curation. Other marketed Brugada genes should be treated skeptically unless current curation supports them.

markers.name: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia panel
markers.description: Pathogenic variants in RYR2 and CASQ2 and related calcium-handling genes can cause CPVT, a high-stakes inherited arrhythmia disorder. Raw DNA cannot rule it out.

markers.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy core gene panel
markers.description: Core sarcomere genes, especially MYH7 and MYBPC3, account for a substantial fraction of genotype-positive HCM in clinical cohorts. This is a clinical panel item, not a consumer SNP trait.

markers.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy core gene panel
markers.impact: Dilated cardiomyopathy / heart failure and arrhythmia susceptibility
markers.description: DCM genetics includes TTN truncating variants, LMNA, MYH7, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, DSP and others. Some genes imply arrhythmic risk beyond ejection fraction. This requires clinical sequencing and cardiology interpretation.

markers.name: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy desmosomal panel
markers.impact: Ventricular arrhythmia and fibro-fatty myocardial remodeling susceptibility
markers.description: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is often rare-variant driven, especially desmosomal genes such as PKP2, DSP, DSG2, DSC2, and JUP. Exercise exposure can modify penetrance in some genotypes.

markers.name: TTR Val142Ile / V122I amyloid cardiomyopathy marker
markers.impact: Destabilized transthyretin tetramer / late-onset ATTR cardiomyopathy susceptibility
markers.description: TTR rs76992529 A encodes p.Val142Ile, a pathogenic variant associated with late-onset hereditary transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, especially but not exclusively in people with African ancestry. Penetrance is age-dependent and incomplete.

markers.name: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection panel
markers.impact: Aortic wall weakness / thoracic aneurysm and dissection susceptibility
markers.description: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection is rare-variant dominated. Validated genes include FBN1, TGFBR1/2, SMAD3, TGFB2, ACTA2, MYH11, MYLK, LOX, PRKG1, and COL3A1. This requires clinical genetics and imaging.

markers.name: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome / COL3A1 panel
markers.description: Pathogenic COL3A1 variants can cause vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, a high-stakes vascular fragility condition. This is not a recreational raw-DNA trait.

markers.name: Aortic aneurysm polygenic susceptibility module
markers.impact: Polygenic aneurysm susceptibility / vascular wall remodeling tendency
markers.description: Abdominal and thoracic aneurysm risk has common-variant components, but imaging and family history dominate. This module should be separate from monogenic HTAAD genes.

markers.name: Calcific aortic valve disease lipid-genetic module
markers.impact: Lp(a)/LDL pathway contribution to aortic valve calcification and stenosis
markers.description: Calcific aortic valve disease has a strong lipid-genetic component, especially LPA/Lp(a). Use LPA variants plus measured Lp(a) and valve imaging when clinically relevant.

markers.name: Bicuspid aortic valve / congenital valve-aorta panel
markers.impact: Congenital valve morphology and aortopathy susceptibility
markers.description: Bicuspid aortic valve and related aortopathy can have familial genetic contributors, including NOTCH1 and SMAD6, but penetrance is variable and echo is the relevant phenotype.

markers.name: Stroke subtype polygenic module
markers.impact: Polygenic ischemic stroke susceptibility by subtype: large artery, cardioembolic, small vessel
markers.description: Stroke genetics is subtype-specific. AF loci influence cardioembolic risk, 9p21/HDAC9 large-artery risk, and COL4A1/2 rare variants small-vessel disease. Do not produce one generic stroke score without subtype caveats.

markers.name: Large-artery ischemic stroke marker
markers.description: HDAC9 rs2107595 A is a replicated ischemic stroke marker, especially for large-artery stroke. It belongs in a stroke-subtype module, not a generic cardiovascular result.

markers.name: Heart failure genetic susceptibility module
markers.impact: Mixed inherited cardiomyopathy, CAD, BP, metabolic, and myocardial-stress burden
markers.description: Heart failure is not one genetic disease. Separate rare cardiomyopathy genes from common CAD/BP/metabolic PRS and from measured cardiac function.

markers.name: Cardiovascular raw DNA interpretation guardrail
markers.impact: Prevents overclaiming from consumer genotype files
markers.description: Raw DNA should not diagnose coronary artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathy, aneurysm, stroke, arrhythmia, hypertension, clotting disorder, or lipid disorder without clinical phenotype. Use DNA to prioritize biomarkers, imaging conversations, family-history review, and pharmacogenomic caution.

markers.name: DNA-to-phenotype cardiovascular validation panel
markers.impact: Prioritizes measurable cardiovascular phenotypes over raw genotype speculation
markers.description: For most cardiovascular genetics, the correct output is a validation checklist: ApoB, LDL-C, Lp(a), fasting triglycerides, blood pressure, glucose/HbA1c, ECG when rhythm/conduction symptoms exist, and CAC or echo only when clinically appropriate.

markers.name: BRCA1 selected pathogenic variant
markers.description: Consumer-array detection of this selected BRCA1 variant is insufficient for clinical interpretation unless current ClinVar/ClinGen classification confirms pathogenicity. Treat as research-only / confirmation-required.

markers.name: BRCA1 selected pathogenic variant
markers.description: Consumer-array detection of this selected BRCA1 variant is insufficient for clinical interpretation unless current ClinVar/ClinGen classification confirms pathogenicity. Treat as research-only / confirmation-required.

markers.name: BRCA2 Lys3326Ter
markers.impact: BRCA2 truncation / double-strand DNA repair compromise
markers.description: ClinVar currently classifies this variant as benign for classic BRCA2-related hereditary breast/ovarian cancer predisposition. It may appear in literature as a low-penetrance modifier, but it must not be reported as a pathogenic BRCA2 mutation.

markers.name: Cancer raw-DNA confirmation rule
markers.description: Any cancer-predisposition result from consumer raw DNA must be treated as unconfirmed until verified by a clinical laboratory. Rare pathogenic variants on SNP arrays are especially vulnerable to false positives, strand/build mismatches, and annotation errors.

markers.name: Variant of uncertain significance non-actionability rule
markers.description: A VUS must not be treated as pathogenic. It may deserve periodic reinterpretation, but it should not trigger prophylactic surgery, intensified screening, or family cascade testing unless reclassified by a qualified clinical source.

markers.name: Negative raw DNA non-reassurance rule
markers.impact: Prevents false reassurance from incomplete consumer genotyping
markers.description: A negative consumer-array result does not rule out hereditary cancer predisposition. Most pathogenic variants are rare, family-specific, structural, copy-number, intronic, or otherwise absent from consumer SNP chips.

markers.name: Somatic tumor mutation non-inference rule
markers.impact: Prevents tumor-genomics claims from germline raw DNA
markers.description: Tumor-driver variants such as EGFR, KRAS, BRAF, ALK, RET, NTRK fusions, MSI status, or tumor mutational burden are usually somatic tumor findings. They cannot be inferred from ordinary germline raw DNA.

markers.name: Cancer polygenic risk score calibration rule
markers.description: Cancer PRS can be useful only when the score is validated for the target ancestry, genotyping platform, imputation method, and clinical model. PRS does not replace monogenic panel testing or standard screening guidelines.

markers.name: BRCA1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: High-penetrance homologous recombination DNA repair cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic/likely pathogenic BRCA1 variants increase risk for hereditary breast/ovarian cancer syndrome and can influence breast, ovarian/fallopian tube/peritoneal, pancreatic, prostate, and therapy-planning discussions.

markers.name: BRCA2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: High-penetrance homologous recombination DNA repair cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic/likely pathogenic BRCA2 variants increase risk for hereditary breast/ovarian cancer syndrome and are also relevant to male breast, pancreatic, prostate, and PARP-inhibitor treatment contexts when tumor criteria apply.

markers.name: BRCA1 c.68_69delAG / 185delAG founder variant
markers.impact: BRCA1 frameshift / hereditary breast-ovarian cancer founder variant
markers.description: BRCA1 c.68_69delAG is a well-known founder pathogenic variant. If present in raw DNA, treat as urgent confirmation-required rather than as a final result.

markers.name: BRCA1 c.5266dupC / 5382insC founder variant
markers.impact: BRCA1 frameshift / hereditary breast-ovarian cancer founder variant
markers.description: BRCA1 c.5266dupC is a well-known founder pathogenic variant. A raw-DNA call should be treated as a clinical confirmation trigger, not a clinical diagnosis.

markers.name: BRCA2 c.5946delT / 6174delT founder variant
markers.impact: BRCA2 frameshift / hereditary breast-ovarian cancer founder variant
markers.description: BRCA2 c.5946delT is a well-known founder pathogenic variant. If seen in raw DNA, confirm with a clinical laboratory and genetic counseling.

markers.name: BRCA1 c.5123C>A / p.Ala1708Glu
markers.impact: BRCA1 missense loss-of-function / hereditary breast-ovarian cancer
markers.description: BRCA1 p.Ala1708Glu is classified as pathogenic by expert curation sources. Raw DNA detection remains confirmation-required.

markers.name: PALB2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Partner/localizer of BRCA2 DNA repair cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic PALB2 variants are associated with clinically meaningful hereditary breast cancer risk and can also be relevant to pancreatic/ovarian risk discussions depending on variant, family history, and guideline context.

markers.name: CHEK2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Moderate-penetrance DNA damage checkpoint cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed CHEK2 pathogenic variants generally confer moderate, variant-specific cancer predisposition, especially breast cancer. Risk differs by variant, zygosity, family history, ancestry, and evolving guidelines.

markers.name: CHEK2 c.1100delC
markers.impact: CHEK2 truncating variant / moderate breast cancer predisposition
markers.description: CHEK2 c.1100delC is a recurrent truncating variant associated with moderate breast cancer predisposition. Raw-DNA detection requires clinical confirmation and variant-specific counseling.

markers.name: CHEK2 p.Ile157Thr / I157T
markers.description: CHEK2 I157T is often interpreted as a lower-penetrance cancer susceptibility allele. It should be reported as a variant-specific modifier, not as equivalent to truncating CHEK2 pathogenic variants.

markers.name: ATM pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: DNA damage response / moderate breast, pancreatic and other cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic ATM variants can confer moderate hereditary cancer predisposition, with risk highly dependent on variant class and family history.

markers.name: TP53 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Li-Fraumeni syndrome
markers.description: Confirmed germline TP53 pathogenic variants are associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome, a high-impact multi-cancer predisposition condition requiring expert management.

markers.name: PTEN pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome
markers.impact: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed PTEN pathogenic variants can indicate PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome, associated with breast, thyroid, endometrial, renal, colorectal, melanoma and benign hamartomatous features.

markers.name: STK11 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
markers.description: Confirmed STK11 pathogenic variants can indicate Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, with gastrointestinal polyps and increased risk for pancreatic, gastrointestinal, breast and gynecologic cancers.

markers.name: CDH1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / hereditary diffuse gastric cancer
markers.impact: E-cadherin loss / diffuse gastric and lobular breast cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed CDH1 pathogenic variants can indicate hereditary diffuse gastric cancer syndrome and lobular breast cancer predisposition. Management can be intensive and must be specialist-led.

markers.name: BARD1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Moderate breast cancer susceptibility / BRCA1-interacting DNA repair gene
markers.description: Confirmed BARD1 pathogenic variants may confer moderate breast cancer predisposition, especially for certain breast cancer subtypes. Risk estimates and management are guideline-dependent.

markers.name: RAD51C pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Homologous recombination DNA repair / ovarian cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed RAD51C pathogenic variants are associated with ovarian cancer predisposition and may also influence breast cancer risk depending on variant and family history.

markers.name: RAD51D pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Homologous recombination DNA repair / ovarian cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed RAD51D pathogenic variants are associated with ovarian cancer predisposition and may influence breast cancer risk in some contexts.

markers.name: BRIP1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.description: Confirmed BRIP1 pathogenic variants are primarily relevant to ovarian cancer predisposition. Breast cancer risk is less clearly actionable than BRCA1/2.

markers.name: NBN pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: DNA repair gene with contested/moderate cancer predisposition evidence
markers.description: NBN has appeared on cancer panels, but penetrance and actionability can be variant- and ancestry-specific. Interpret only with current clinical guidelines and ClinGen/ClinVar status.

markers.name: NF1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Neurofibromatosis type 1 tumor predisposition and breast cancer context
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic NF1 variants cause neurofibromatosis type 1, a tumor predisposition syndrome with malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor risk and breast cancer screening implications in some adults.

markers.name: MLH1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Lynch syndrome
markers.description: Confirmed germline MLH1 pathogenic variants indicate Lynch syndrome, increasing risk for colorectal, endometrial and other Lynch-associated cancers.

markers.name: MSH2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Lynch syndrome
markers.description: Confirmed germline MSH2 pathogenic variants indicate Lynch syndrome, with colorectal, endometrial, ovarian, urinary tract and other Lynch-associated cancer risks.

markers.name: MSH6 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Lynch syndrome
markers.impact: Mismatch repair loss / Lynch syndrome, often later-onset/variable penetrance
markers.description: Confirmed germline MSH6 pathogenic variants indicate Lynch syndrome, often with strong endometrial cancer relevance and variable colorectal cancer penetrance.

markers.name: PMS2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Lynch syndrome
markers.impact: Mismatch repair loss / lower-penetrance Lynch syndrome gene
markers.description: Confirmed germline PMS2 pathogenic variants indicate Lynch syndrome, generally with lower and later-onset penetrance than MLH1/MSH2, but still clinically relevant.

markers.name: EPCAM deletion panel / Lynch syndrome via MSH2 silencing
markers.description: Certain germline EPCAM deletions can silence neighboring MSH2 and cause Lynch syndrome. This is a structural variant problem, not a typical SNP problem.

markers.name: APC pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / familial adenomatous polyposis
markers.impact: Wnt pathway dysregulation / adenomatous polyposis and colorectal cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed APC pathogenic variants can cause familial adenomatous polyposis or attenuated FAP, with very high colorectal adenoma burden and cancer risk without surveillance/management.

markers.name: APC p.Ile1307Lys / I1307K
markers.impact: Moderate colorectal cancer risk modifier, ancestry-contextual
markers.description: APC I1307K is a moderate colorectal cancer risk allele, especially described in Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry. It does not cause classic FAP by itself.

markers.name: MUTYH-associated polyposis biallelic pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Base-excision repair defect / autosomal recessive adenomatous polyposis
markers.description: Biallelic MUTYH pathogenic variants can cause MUTYH-associated polyposis. Monoallelic carrier status has much weaker and context-dependent risk implications; clinical confirmation is required.

markers.name: MUTYH p.Tyr179Cys / Y179C
markers.impact: MUTYH pathogenic founder variant; MAP risk mainly when biallelic/compound heterozygous
markers.description: MUTYH Y179C is a recurrent pathogenic variant. Interpretation depends heavily on whether another pathogenic MUTYH variant is present in trans.

markers.name: MUTYH p.Gly396Asp / G396D
markers.impact: MUTYH pathogenic founder variant; MAP risk mainly when biallelic/compound heterozygous
markers.description: MUTYH G396D is a recurrent pathogenic variant. The key clinical question is monoallelic carrier status versus biallelic/compound heterozygous MAP.

markers.name: Polymerase proofreading-associated polyposis panel
markers.impact: DNA polymerase proofreading defect / colorectal and endometrial cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic variants in the exonuclease/proofreading domains of POLE or POLD1 can predispose to colorectal polyposis/cancer and endometrial cancer.

markers.name: NTHL1 tumor syndrome biallelic pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Base-excision repair defect / recessive adenomatous polyposis and multi-tumor syndrome
markers.description: Biallelic NTHL1 pathogenic variants can cause an adenomatous polyposis and multi-tumor predisposition syndrome. Monoallelic status is not equivalent.

markers.name: GREM1 duplication / hereditary mixed polyposis syndrome
markers.impact: BMP pathway dysregulation / mixed colorectal polyposis predisposition
markers.description: Certain GREM1 duplications are associated with hereditary mixed polyposis syndrome and colorectal cancer predisposition.

markers.name: SMAD4 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / juvenile polyposis ± HHT
markers.impact: TGF-beta pathway tumor predisposition / juvenile polyposis syndrome
markers.description: Confirmed SMAD4 pathogenic variants can cause juvenile polyposis syndrome and may overlap with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia features.

markers.name: BMPR1A pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / juvenile polyposis
markers.impact: BMP receptor pathway / juvenile polyposis syndrome
markers.description: Confirmed BMPR1A pathogenic variants can cause juvenile polyposis syndrome with gastrointestinal polyp and colorectal/gastric cancer implications.

markers.name: RET pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / MEN2
markers.impact: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 / medullary thyroid cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed activating germline RET pathogenic variants can indicate MEN2, with medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma risk. Variant-specific codon risk matters.

markers.name: MEN1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 tumor predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed MEN1 pathogenic variants can indicate MEN1, with parathyroid, pituitary and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor predisposition.

markers.name: VHL pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.description: Confirmed VHL pathogenic variants can indicate von Hippel-Lindau disease, associated with renal cell carcinoma, hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma and pancreatic lesions.

markers.name: FH pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / HLRCC
markers.impact: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed FH pathogenic variants can indicate HLRCC, with cutaneous/uterine leiomyomas and aggressive renal cell carcinoma risk. Specialist renal surveillance is important.

markers.name: FLCN pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / Birt-Hogg-Dube
markers.impact: Birt-Hogg-Dube renal tumor and pneumothorax predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed FLCN pathogenic variants can indicate Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome, with renal tumor risk, lung cysts/spontaneous pneumothorax, and fibrofolliculomas.

markers.name: BAP1 tumor predisposition syndrome panel
markers.impact: Uveal melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cell carcinoma and cutaneous tumor predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed BAP1 pathogenic variants can indicate BAP1 tumor predisposition syndrome, relevant to uveal melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cell carcinoma and BAP1-inactivated melanocytic tumors.

markers.name: CDKN2A pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.impact: Familial melanoma and pancreatic cancer predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed CDKN2A pathogenic variants can indicate familial melanoma predisposition and pancreatic cancer risk in some families.

markers.name: MITF p.Glu318Lys / E318K
markers.impact: Melanoma and renal cell carcinoma susceptibility modifier
markers.description: MITF E318K is a moderate/low-penetrance susceptibility variant reported in melanoma and renal cancer contexts. It is not a deterministic cancer syndrome marker.

markers.name: MC1R p.Arg151Cys / R151C
markers.description: MC1R R151C is a red-hair/fair-skin pigmentation allele that can contribute to melanoma susceptibility through UV sensitivity and pigmentation biology. It is not a melanoma diagnosis marker.

markers.name: MC1R p.Arg160Trp / R160W
markers.description: MC1R R160W is a pigmentation allele associated with red-hair/fair-skin biology and melanoma susceptibility context, but it is not independently diagnostic.

markers.name: MC1R p.Asp294His / D294H
markers.description: MC1R D294H is a red-hair/fair-skin pigmentation allele and melanoma-context risk modifier, not a clinical cancer predisposition diagnosis.

markers.name: SDHB pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.description: Confirmed SDHB pathogenic variants can indicate hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma syndrome, with notable metastatic potential and renal/GIST associations.

markers.name: SDHD pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.description: Confirmed SDHD pathogenic variants can indicate hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma syndrome, often with parent-of-origin/inheritance nuance.

markers.name: MAX/TMEM127 pathogenic variant panel
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic variants in MAX or TMEM127 can predispose to pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma, with gene-specific penetrance and management.

markers.name: DICER1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel
markers.description: Confirmed DICER1 pathogenic variants can predispose to pleuropulmonary blastoma, thyroid tumors, ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors and other tumor types, often with pediatric/family implications.

markers.name: RB1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant panel / hereditary retinoblastoma
markers.description: Confirmed germline RB1 pathogenic variants can indicate hereditary retinoblastoma predisposition and secondary malignancy risk. This is pediatric high-stakes.

markers.name: Tuberous sclerosis complex tumor predisposition panel
markers.impact: Hamartoma/tumor predisposition involving kidney, brain, lung and skin
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic variants in TSC1 or TSC2 can indicate tuberous sclerosis complex, with angiomyolipoma, subependymal giant cell astrocytoma and other tumor/hamartoma risks.

markers.name: Gorlin syndrome / basal cell nevus syndrome panel
markers.description: Confirmed PTCH1 or SUFU pathogenic variants can indicate basal cell nevus/Gorlin syndrome, with basal cell carcinoma, jaw keratocysts and medulloblastoma risk nuances.

markers.name: Rhabdoid tumor / small-cell ovarian hypercalcemic type predisposition panel
markers.description: Confirmed pathogenic variants in SMARCB1 or SMARCA4 can indicate rare but serious tumor predisposition syndromes. Age, gene, tumor type, and family history are among the factors that inform management.

markers.name: Familial neuroblastoma predisposition panel
markers.impact: Neuroblastoma predisposition / neural crest tumor biology
markers.description: Confirmed germline pathogenic variants in ALK or PHOX2B can contribute to familial neuroblastoma predisposition. This is rare and typically pediatric/family-history driven.

markers.name: RUNX1 familial platelet disorder with myeloid malignancy predisposition
markers.impact: Inherited platelet disorder and leukemia predisposition
