markers.description: Confirmed germline RUNX1 pathogenic variants can predispose to platelet disorders and myeloid malignancies. Distinguishing germline from somatic hematologic findings is critical.

markers.name: DDX41 myeloid neoplasm predisposition panel
markers.impact: Adult-onset myelodysplastic syndrome / acute myeloid leukemia predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed germline DDX41 pathogenic variants can predispose to adult-onset myeloid neoplasms. Family history may be subtle due to later onset.

markers.name: CEBPA familial AML predisposition panel
markers.description: Confirmed germline CEBPA pathogenic variants can predispose to familial AML. Interpretation must distinguish germline variants from somatic leukemia mutations.

markers.name: GATA2 deficiency / myeloid malignancy predisposition panel
markers.impact: Immunodeficiency, marrow failure and myeloid malignancy predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed germline GATA2 pathogenic variants can cause immunodeficiency/marrow failure syndromes with myeloid malignancy risk.

markers.name: Inherited thrombocytopenia and leukemia predisposition panel
markers.impact: Platelet disorder and hematologic malignancy predisposition
markers.description: Confirmed germline ANKRD26 or ETV6 pathogenic variants can predispose to inherited thrombocytopenia and hematologic malignancies.

markers.name: HOXB13 p.Gly84Glu / G84E
markers.description: HOXB13 G84E is a prostate cancer susceptibility allele with ancestry-specific frequency and risk. It is not diagnostic and does not replace PSA/family-history based screening decisions.

markers.name: Prostate cancer polygenic risk score module
markers.description: Validated prostate cancer PRS can stratify inherited susceptibility, but it does not diagnose cancer and must be calibrated by ancestry, family history and clinical screening context.

markers.name: Breast cancer PRS313-style module
markers.description: A validated PRS313-style breast cancer score can add risk stratification beyond family history and monogenic testing, but only if ancestry, platform and model calibration are appropriate.

markers.name: Colorectal cancer polygenic risk score module
markers.description: A validated colorectal cancer PRS can stratify population risk and may eventually inform screening timing, but it does not replace colonoscopy findings, family history, or hereditary syndrome testing.

markers.name: Melanoma pigmentation and nevus-count PRS module
markers.description: Pigmentation/nevi polygenic burden can contextualize melanoma susceptibility, but dermatologic phenotype and UV exposure are more actionable than a raw PRS.

markers.name: 8q24 rs6983267 colorectal/prostate cancer susceptibility locus
markers.impact: Common low-effect enhancer-region cancer susceptibility marker
markers.description: 8q24 rs6983267 is a replicated common susceptibility locus in colorectal/prostate cancer research, but its individual predictive value is small and PRS-dependent.

markers.name: FGFR2 rs2981582 breast cancer susceptibility locus
markers.impact: Common low-effect breast cancer susceptibility marker
markers.description: FGFR2 rs2981582 is a replicated common breast cancer GWAS locus. It belongs in a PRS context, not as a stand-alone clinical cancer risk finding.

markers.name: TOX3 rs3803662 breast cancer susceptibility locus
markers.impact: Common low-effect breast cancer susceptibility marker
markers.description: TOX3 rs3803662 is a replicated common breast cancer susceptibility locus, but the individual SNP is not clinically actionable by itself.

markers.name: MAP3K1 rs889312 breast cancer susceptibility locus
markers.impact: Common low-effect breast cancer susceptibility marker
markers.description: MAP3K1 rs889312 is a common low-effect breast cancer GWAS marker. It is appropriate for PRS calculations, not stand-alone risk reporting.

markers.name: MSMB rs10993994 prostate cancer susceptibility locus
markers.impact: Common low-effect prostate cancer susceptibility marker
markers.description: MSMB rs10993994 is a replicated prostate cancer GWAS locus. It belongs in a calibrated prostate PRS, not as a stand-alone clinical finding.

markers.name: UGT1A1*28 TA-repeat promoter variant
markers.impact: Reduced UGT1A1 glucuronidation / irinotecan toxicity risk context
markers.description: UGT1A1*28/*28 can increase irinotecan toxicity risk, especially neutropenia/diarrhea, depending on irinotecan dose and regimen. Use oncology pharmacogenomic guidance.

markers.name: CYP2D6 tamoxifen activation phenotype panel
markers.description: CYP2D6 metabolizer status may affect tamoxifen activation, but treatment decisions require oncology context, menopausal status, drug interactions and current guideline interpretation.

markers.name: Hereditary pancreatic cancer context panel
markers.impact: Pancreatic cancer predisposition across multiple syndromes
markers.description: Pancreatic cancer susceptibility can arise from several hereditary syndromes. The same gene may imply different surveillance depending on family history and guideline criteria.

markers.name: Hereditary prostate cancer context panel
markers.impact: Inherited prostate cancer susceptibility across DNA repair and HOXB13 genes
markers.description: Hereditary prostate cancer risk can involve BRCA2, BRCA1, ATM, CHEK2, HOXB13 and mismatch repair genes. Gene-specific risk and screening guidance differ.

markers.name: Hereditary renal cancer context panel
markers.impact: Inherited renal tumor predisposition across multiple syndromes
markers.description: Hereditary renal cancer risk can involve VHL, FH, FLCN, BAP1, MET, SDHB, TSC1/TSC2, PTEN and other genes. Histology and syndrome features matter.

markers.name: Hereditary endometrial cancer context panel
markers.impact: Inherited endometrial cancer susceptibility across Lynch, PTEN and polymerase genes
markers.description: Hereditary endometrial cancer risk is strongly linked to Lynch syndrome genes and can also involve PTEN and polymerase proofreading genes. Tumor testing may guide germline evaluation.

markers.name: Hereditary ovarian cancer context panel
markers.impact: Inherited ovarian cancer susceptibility across homologous recombination and Lynch genes
markers.description: Hereditary ovarian cancer risk can involve BRCA1/2, RAD51C, RAD51D, BRIP1, PALB2 and Lynch genes. Gene-specific penetrance and management differ.

markers.name: Childhood cancer predisposition context panel
markers.impact: Pediatric tumor predisposition across multiple high-impact genes
markers.description: Some hereditary cancer syndromes primarily affect children or have pediatric-onset surveillance implications. Any raw-DNA signal here should be treated as urgent confirmation-required.

markers.name: Family history override rule for hereditary cancer evaluation
markers.impact: Clinical triage rule when raw DNA is negative or incomplete
markers.description: Strong personal or family history can justify clinical hereditary cancer evaluation even when consumer raw DNA is negative. Raw SNP absence must not override pedigree, tumor type, young age at diagnosis, bilateral/multiple primaries, or known familial variants.

markers.name: Allergy genotype non-diagnostic rule
markers.description: Allergic disease requires exposure history and immune testing. Genotype can suggest predisposition, but it cannot diagnose allergy, anaphylaxis risk, MCAS, or food intolerance by itself.

markers.name: Atopy / allergic disease PRS module
markers.description: Atopy, allergic rhinitis, eczema, asthma, and IgE tendency are polygenic and environmentally triggered. Use only as a calibrated PRS module with ancestry-aware interpretation.

markers.name: Mast-cell mediator and activation context panel
markers.impact: Mast-cell activation and mediator biology context
markers.description: Mast-cell disorders and hereditary alpha-tryptasemia are not reliably inferred from ordinary SNP arrays. Use this as a callability/triage panel requiring validated testing when symptoms fit.

markers.name: Ile50Val / IL4R alpha variant
markers.description: IL4R regulates IL-4 and IL-13 signaling, central to allergic inflammation and IgE class switching. This variant is a context marker for atopy/asthma tendency, not an allergy test.

markers.name: Gln576Arg
markers.description: IL4R Gln576Arg has been studied in atopy and asthma phenotypes. Treat as a pathway marker for Th2 tone and airway/allergy context.

markers.name: Arg130Gln
markers.description: IL13 is a key Th2 cytokine. rs20541 has been repeatedly studied for asthma, IgE, and atopy-related phenotypes, but effect sizes are modest.

markers.name: -590C>T promoter
markers.impact: IL-4 expression / IgE class switching context
markers.description: IL4 promoter variation can modify Th2 cytokine expression and IgE tendency in some cohorts. Use as a weak context marker only.

markers.name: 17q21 asthma-associated locus
markers.description: The 17q21 ORMDL3/GSDMB region is a robust asthma susceptibility locus. It is not specific to allergy and should be interpreted with respiratory symptoms.

markers.name: TSLP epithelial alarmin locus
markers.description: TSLP is an epithelial cytokine involved in initiating allergic inflammation. Common variants are useful as atopy/asthma context markers.

markers.name: High-affinity IgE receptor alpha promoter
markers.description: FCER1A encodes a component of the high-affinity IgE receptor. Variation can modify total IgE and allergic sensitization tendency.

markers.name: Filaggrin loss-of-function skin barrier panel
markers.impact: Skin barrier disruption / eczema and food sensitization risk
markers.description: Filaggrin loss-of-function variants can strongly influence atopic dermatitis and skin barrier dysfunction. Consumer SNP files may include only selected FLG variants and cannot rule out FLG loss-of-function.

markers.name: IL2RA immune-regulatory locus
markers.description: IL2RA variants are immune-regulatory markers relevant across autoimmune and allergic immune tone. Use only as broad immune context.

markers.name: IL33 receptor pathway asthma/allergy locus
markers.description: IL1RL1 participates in IL-33 signaling, an epithelial alarmin pathway involved in asthma and allergic inflammation.

markers.name: IL33 allergic airway locus
markers.description: IL33 variants appear in allergic airway and asthma GWAS. Useful as pathway context, not individual prediction.

markers.name: GSDMB asthma locus
markers.impact: Airway inflammation and asthma susceptibility locus
markers.description: GSDMB is part of the 17q21 asthma locus. Treat as a small-effect respiratory/allergy context marker.

markers.name: GSDMA asthma/allergy locus
markers.description: Gasdermin loci are associated with asthma and inflammatory airway traits. Individual interpretation requires phenotype.

markers.name: Th2 cytokine-region allergy locus
markers.description: RAD50 lies near Th2 cytokine genes and has appeared in allergy/asthma association studies. Treat as locus-level context only.

markers.name: HLA food/immune sensitivity context
markers.impact: HLA-mediated food and immune reaction context
markers.description: HLA alleles contribute to many immune reactions, but tagging SNPs are unreliable. Use this only as a prompt to require true HLA typing for celiac, drug, or allergy-related questions.

markers.name: Hereditary angioedema confirmation panel
markers.description: Hereditary angioedema is not an IgE allergy and is not ruled out by SNP arrays. Use as a red-flag panel for recurrent swelling without hives.

markers.name: Leukotriene C4 synthase promoter
markers.description: LTC4S is involved in leukotriene synthesis and has been studied in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease and asthma medication response.

markers.name: Low-affinity IgE receptor / asthma medication context
markers.impact: IgE receptor and asthma controller response context
markers.description: FCER2 has been studied in IgE regulation and asthma controller response. Not useful without asthma phenotype and medication history.

markers.description: Chronic urticaria is usually not explained by one SNP. Use this panel to prompt phenotype questions and clinician testing.

markers.description: Eczema risk combines skin barrier, immune signaling, microbiome, irritants, and allergens. Use as a context panel with skin phenotype.

markers.impact: Pollen, dust mite, mold sensitization context
markers.description: Inhalant allergy is best confirmed by exposure-linked symptoms and IgE/skin testing. Genetics can only raise or lower prior plausibility.

markers.name: Digestive genotype non-diagnostic rule
markers.description: Digestive symptoms require phenotype, labs, diet history, and sometimes endoscopy or breath testing. Genotype cannot diagnose IBS, IBD, celiac disease, food allergy, or microbiome status.

markers.name: Celiac HLA-DQ2/DQ8 typing panel

markers.name: Inflammatory bowel disease PRS module
markers.impact: Crohn disease / ulcerative colitis genetic susceptibility context
markers.description: IBD risk is polygenic and immune-microbiome-environment mediated. Use calibrated PRS only as context with symptoms and inflammatory markers.

markers.name: Arg702Trp
markers.impact: Crohn disease innate immune risk modifier
markers.description: NOD2 variants are among the best-known Crohn disease susceptibility markers, especially in European ancestry. They are not diagnostic without GI phenotype.

markers.name: Gly908Arg
markers.impact: Crohn disease innate immune risk modifier
markers.description: NOD2 Gly908Arg is a Crohn disease susceptibility marker. Interpret only with ancestry and GI/inflammatory phenotype.

markers.name: Leu1007fsinsC
markers.description: NOD2 Leu1007fs is a high-priority Crohn susceptibility variant but still cannot diagnose IBD from raw DNA alone.

markers.name: Thr300Ala
markers.description: ATG16L1 is involved in autophagy and intestinal immune handling. rs2241880 is a replicated Crohn disease locus with modest effect.

markers.name: Arg381Gln
markers.description: IL23R variation modifies IBD susceptibility through Th17 immune signaling. Direction and effect should be checked against ancestry and model.

markers.name: Non-European lactase persistence variant panel
markers.description: Lactase persistence is driven by different regulatory variants across populations. A single European marker can miss non-European lactase persistence alleles.

markers.name: D19H gallstone / sterol transport variant
markers.description: ABCG8 D19H is associated with gallstone susceptibility and sterol transport differences. Confirm with symptoms and imaging, not DNA alone.

markers.name: Sterol transporter locus

markers.name: Fructose/FODMAP tolerance context panel
markers.description: FODMAP sensitivity is mostly phenotype/microbiome/dose driven. Genetic data is weak except rare fructose metabolism disorders requiring clinical testing.

markers.name: ALDOB hereditary fructose intolerance panel

markers.name: Bile acid and gallbladder context panel
markers.impact: Bile flow, gallstones, and fat-digestion context
markers.description: Bile-related symptoms require phenotype and imaging. Genetics can provide context around sterol transport and bile composition.

markers.name: Host glycan microbiome context panel
markers.description: Host genetics can shape microbiome niches, but raw DNA cannot tell someone their microbiome composition. Use stool testing only when clinically useful.

markers.description: No genotype makes someone destined or unable to build muscle, endurance, power, or athletic skill. Genetics can suggest training bias and recovery context only.
